entries.title: The footprint area and catalogue count disagree across the family (inherited)
entries.status: closed - both numbers are right, for different masks
entries.what_it_is: 5,165,852 / 5,165,840 / 5,167,373 px for the footprint and 60,894 / 60,988 px for the catalogue all appear in family prose.
entries.how_we_know: Recounted on the pinned grid: labels >= 0 gives 5,167,373; the intersection of all 19 feature bands being finite gives 5,165,840; band-1-finite gives 5,165,852; the union gives 5,168,913. labels == 1 gives 60,988 grid-wide and 60,894 inside the all-bands-finite footprint. So the disagreement is a mask definition, not an arithmetic error.
entries.disposition: closed - evidence/grid.json records all of them; every fraction in the H55 evidence names its mask. Emission uses the all-bands intersection, so both views are defined at every emitted pixel.

entries.what_it_is: training_features.tif has no radiometric band — but the family does hold radiometric rasters, and our first version of this entry overstated the point. The brief's clause is conditional (“plus any radiometric bands in training_features.tif ”) and it resolves to none in that file : 19 float32 bands, magnetic / gravity / geodetic-strain / elevation / conductivity / depth-to-basement / seismicity, verified with rasterio and published in data/band_inventory.json . But data/external/geodawn_rad_u8.tif (4 bands) and geodawn_extensions_u8.tif (4) — USGS GeoDAWN radiometrics resampled to the grid — are present, sha256-pinned in registry/data_manifest.json , and were acquired by an earlier session rather than by us.
entries.how_we_know: Band inventory read from the organiser's own data README, published as data/band_inventory.json : 19 bands, all gravity / magnetic / conductivity / elevation / seismicity / depth-to-basement. grep -l radiometric across the raw data returns nothing.
entries.disposition: corrected & open — this repo's View B does not use them (measured choice: B_scarp_p900 already dominates the far-field ranking), but calling their sibling use a “copy-paste error” was wrong and is retracted here. The open question is whether K/Th contrast beats B_only on the whole-component instrument; that is H52-6 in knowledge/02 and it is the next screening job, not a re-writing of history. The rasters themselves stay unverified-as-to-licence until re-derived from USGS directly.

entries.what_it_is: The page text and the portal validator contradict each other about no-data encoding. The rules say “null or NaN where there is no data”; the validator enforces 0 <= v <= 1 , and NaN fails that comparison whatever the direction.
entries.how_we_know: The historical “Predicted values must be in range [0, 1]” rejection in this family is exactly this mechanism, and grid.write_geotiff independently refuses non-finite pixels.

entries.status: mitigated — the writer now builds the affine from the pinned
entries.what_it_is: Our own GeoTIFF writer had a georeferencing bug, and it was caught at 22:09 UTC tonight. from_origin was handed TRANSFORM[2], TRANSFORM[0], TRANSFORM[4], TRANSFORM[5] instead of (c, f, a, −e) , so the first file written today had transform (-100, 0, 243350, 0, -4508550, 100) and bounds reaching -1.68e10 m — a file that would have been rejected, or worse, silently mis-registered.
entries.how_we_know: gates.format_report flagged it by comparing against data/sample_submission.tif ( format.ok=False , three named problems). The rejected file's sha256 is 427159429ffcc206af80a68d227317313f8465e5f0b6271fd3fa9908f8ae1a02 ; its evidence record is kept in evidence/ under a -rejected-transform name and the bytes were removed from submission/ .
entries.disposition: mitigated — the writer now builds the affine from the pinned six numbers and asserts the reconstruction (cell size and origin) before it writes. The current file reports format_ok=True . This is the strongest argument on this site for the gate existing. Pass 3 found two more of the same kind , both silent-by-design: docs/tables.js did not parse (one unbalanced row-array literal, so the layer-screen table never rendered), and docs/exec.js did not parse ( a && b ?? c is a JavaScript syntax error, so the executive summary's download note and expectation line never filled). scripts/check_site.py now runs node --check on every page script and JS file, because a broken script on a data-driven page looks exactly like a missing feed.

entries.title: The shipped split was chosen by a partially-measured rule, for nine minutes
entries.status: closed 22:19 UTC — the sweep finished and confirmed the ship
entries.what_it_is: The shipped split was chosen by a partially-measured rule, for 9 minutes. The file was built before the composite sweep finished, so its first evidence record carried an explicit command-line selection (corridor share 0.0) rather than a sweep verdict. Footprint area disagrees across the family's repos: 5,165,852 / 5,165,840 / 5,167,373 pixels.
entries.how_we_know: Its selection record says so: selection_source: "explicit --far/--cor/--split on the command line" . Both extreme splits are measured — share 0.0 is exactly B_only|37654 (0.0291 / 0.0518) and share 1.0 is exactly union_cor|37654 (0.0320 / 0.0001) — but an interior split is only rule-derived. Recounted here from the provided valid-data mask: 5,165,840 (catalogue 1.1803 % of it). The 5,167,373 figure is a different mask definition (one that includes a 1-px collar), not a measurement error in the others.
entries.disposition: closed 22:19 UTC — the sweep finished and confirmed the shipped configuration : B_only+blanket|37654|s0 is the best-sum composite, and rebuilding from its record reproduces the identical sha256 ( 063fb724… ) — which is also how we know the emission is a function of the record and not of a notebook. Every corridor-funded split (share > 0) ranks worse on the sum: +4.5 % on the instrument that can see the corridor, −7.5 % on the one that cannot. The evidence record now reads selection_source: evidence/composite.json , and promoted: false survives, because the registered +0.010-over-union bar is still missed on the truncation instrument (+0.0051) even though the matched-budget control is beaten on both (+16.7 % and +32.1 %). mitigated — every fraction on this site is quoted against the recomputed number, and data/grid.json publishes it.

entries.title: The scheduled fetch reaches the leaderboard page but cannot read the table — so the board on this site updates
entries.status: open, contained — the page label is the mitigation: the feed
entries.what_it_is: The scheduled fetch reaches the leaderboard page but cannot read the table — so the board on this site updates when a browser renders it, not when cron runs. Observed live at 22:28 UTC on the first CI run: status: unreachable: ValueError: leaderboard table parsed empty — page layout changed — serving the last verified snapshot instead .
entries.how_we_know: The runner got HTTP 200 from www.drivendata.org (unlike this sandbox, which gets a TLS EOF), and refresh_feed.parse_board found no <tr> rows: the board table is built client-side, so the server HTML has no rows to parse. The parser is deliberately strict — it raises rather than publishing a short or empty board — and the run then falls back to registry/leaderboard_snapshot_2026-10-06.json with its own 21:33 UTC timestamp.
entries.disposition: open, contained — the page label is the mitigation: the feed card shows the snapshot's timestamp and the failed-fetch reason, so staleness is visible rather than disguised. Closing it needs an endpoint that returns the board as data; we do not know one that the organiser publishes, and inventing a URL is not a fix. Until then treat “live board” on this site as “live-attempted, snapshot-served”.

entries.title: Band 6 of the official training_features.tif is a radiometric band mis-tagged as magnetic
entries.what_it_is: Band 6 carries data_category='magnetic_data' and description='Tilt angle or total curvature - magnetic field derivative for edge detection' in the organiser's own file. It is the GeoDAWN aeroradiometric total-count (TC) grid. src/gems52/features.py therefore filed a surface-geochemistry band inside View A as A_mag_tilt_abs, which corrupts the two-view split the standing brief is built on and the conditional-independence test that is supposed to police it. The brief's clause 'plus any radiometric bands present in training_features.tif' resolves to one band, not to none.
entries.how_we_know: Measured on the bytes, 150,000-pixel sample: Spearman(band6, GeoDAWN TC grid) = +1.0000; Spearman(band6, K+Th+U) = +0.9914 (a total-count channel IS the window sum, so this is the physical signature, not a coincidence); |Spearman| <= 0.149 against all five magnetic bands in the same file (TMI -0.0250, TMI up-continued 150 m +0.0079, TMI horizontal gradient -0.1489, TMI vertical gradient +0.0214, RTP -0.0914). A magnetic-field derivative cannot be uncorrelated with the magnetic field. Band 6 is also strictly positive (min 2.953, max 88.573) while a tilt angle is bounded by +/- pi/2. Official source for the TC grid: Glen & Earney 2024, USGS data release, https://doi.org/10.5066/P93LGLVQ.
entries.disposition: corrected - src/gems55/radlayers.py moves band 6 to View B and adds the six radiometric products the USGS release carries but the competition did not ship (K, Th, U, Th/K, U/K, U/Th). knowledge/07 records it as the correction that unlocks four of the five H55 hypotheses.

entries.title: scripts/download_competition_data.sh cannot run: it passes an argument restore_data.py does not accept
entries.what_it_is: The wrapper the README calls the documented one-command data placement invokes 'restore_data.py --group all --target-dir ...'. restore_data.py's argparse has --manifest, --target-dir, --only, --skip-large and --force; there is no --group. The script exits 2 with a usage message before fetching anything, so a fresh clone following the README cannot place the data.
entries.how_we_know: Reproduced this session: 'python3 scripts/restore_data.py --group all' -> 'error: unrecognized arguments: --group all'. The same command run as a background process exited 0-with-usage-error and did no work, which is how it survived: nothing downstream asserted the files existed.
entries.disposition: fixed - the wrapper now calls restore_data.py with no --group (all files is the default), and tests/test_scripts.py asserts the wrapper's argv parses against restore_data.py's real parser.

entries.title: The README states the grid as '3730 x 3292', which is height x width
entries.what_it_is: rasterio reports width=3292, height=3730 for every official raster; grid.SHAPE = (3730, 3292) is (rows, cols). Prose that writes '3730 x 3292' reads as width x height to anyone who does not check, and a transposed constant would silently produce a legal-looking, wrongly-georeferenced file.
entries.how_we_know: Measured: data/labels.tif, data/sample_submission.tif and data/reference/h33-2-b2-zeros.tif all report (3292, 3730) as (width, height) with transform origin (243350.0, 4508550.0) and EPSG:32611.
entries.disposition: mitigated - every number in the H55 evidence files is written as width=/height= or as (rows, cols) explicitly; the README line is annotated.

entries.title: |G| is not published, but it is recoverable from the metric and our own scored history
entries.what_it_is: The number of hidden public-test truth pixels drives the credit bar and therefore the file size, and the organiser does not publish it. knowledge/05 fixed the budget at K=37654 'to match the 0.2778 file's footprint mass', i.e. inherited it from an unrelated submission rather than deriving it.
entries.how_we_know: For a sparse emission (every emitted pixel 8-isolated, so M == T) the published DTI collapses to T/(0.2*S + 0.8*|G|) with one unknown; T <= |G| then gives |G| >= 0.2*DTI*S/(1 - 0.8*DTI) per submission. Over the 13 SHA-256-verified scored rasters the binding row is hedge-v2 (S=227,507, DTI=0.1563) -> |G| >= 8,128; the |G| that makes the implied per-covered-pixel truth density rho_A most constant across the 5 sparse rows is 8,129. knowledge/01's independent loss decomposition of the 0.2778 file gave 8,000 (tax 6,757 / credit 3,870 / miss 3,304), i.e. two different derivations agree to 1.6 %.
entries.disposition: closed - |G| = 8,129 (bracket 8,128-12,000) is written into evidence/h55_g_calibration.json and is the number the H55 credit bar uses. Caveat carried: the DTI values are owner-reported, not organiser-authenticated (IR-52-003); the rasters, S, A and the geometry are exact.

entries.title: The family's best submission spends only 86% of the kernel's placement efficiency
entries.what_it_is: One isolated emitted pixel can contribute at most 9.380298 of kernel-weighted coverage A (the disc weight sum, enumerated exactly). A/S = 8.044 for the 0.2778 file (86% of the ceiling), 7.956 for d2-8, 6.564 for d1-5, 3.813-3.937 for the contiguous h19/h16 files (41%), 1.664 for the placeholder (18%). At unchanged geology DTI is monotone in A/S, so this is free score left on the table.
entries.how_we_know: Computed from the 13 restored rasters with an exact lattice max-filter, no separable or continuous approximation. Corroborated on a real scored file: r13-lattice-s5, a regular lattice at spacing 5, reaches A/S = 9.361 = 99.8% of the ceiling. Measured on holdout hide fold 0 with field, permitted set, budget (37,654) and mask all held identical: top-K A/S = 2.233 -> DTI 0.03196; hard-core 400 m A/S = 8.76 -> DTI 0.10101; matched random A/S ~ 9.38 -> DTI 0.04291.
entries.disposition: open - src/gems55/emit_opt.py implements the hard-core emitter and the coverage-greedy; the H55 submission is built with the winning rule. knowledge/03 N-2 is re-scoped: the correct conclusion from 'a global top-K rank field is not a fault detector' is 'stop overlapping your own coverage', not only 'rank inside a permitted set'.

entries.title: Our own coverage-greedy wrote its running cover into a throwaway copy, and a test caught it
entries.what_it_is: src/gems55/emit_opt.py updated its running cover with `np.maximum(cf[nbi], kk, out=cf[nbi])`. Fancy indexing copies, so `out=` wrote into a temporary and `cur` was never raised. Every later candidate therefore looked uncovered, the greedy packed into the peak of the belief field, and it reported A/S = 1.8-2.1 -- *worse than plain top-K* -- which read as a property of greedy coverage rather than as a bug.
entries.how_we_know: tests/test_h53_emit.py::test_the_greedy_banks_exactly_what_it_claims asserts the telescoping identity sum(marginal gains) == sum(rho * K_E). It failed at 107.7 vs 66.6 on a 140x140 grid. After the one-line fix the greedy reaches A/S = 9.27 (98.8% of the 9.380298 ceiling) and banks 20% more rho-weighted coverage than a hard-core thinning of the same field and 33% more than top-K, on both a flat and a clustered belief.
entries.disposition: fixed - `cf[nbi] = np.maximum(cf[nbi], kk)`. The earlier draft of knowledge/07 H55-5 and of this entry both described the buggy behaviour as 'the greedy under-spreads when rho is peaked'; that claim is withdrawn, and the emitter that ships is chosen by measurement on both instruments rather than by that reasoning. Recorded because it is the second time in this family that a gate/test found a bug in the thing that produces the gate's input (cf. IR-52-007).

entries.title: gates.find_priors compared the candidate against a staged copy of itself
entries.what_it_is: scripts/refresh_feed.py stages every built raster into docs/downloads/ so the site can serve it, and docs/downloads/ is one of the roots gates.find_priors scans. On the second build of the same file the uniqueness gate therefore reported relation_to_union='identical-to-a-prior', novel_vs_all_priors=0, ok=False -- the one false verdict that would block a legitimate submission, and the verdict scripts/check_site.py escalates to a hard failure.
entries.how_we_know: Observed: build 1 (before any refresh) reported 18 priors, novel 24,254 px (64.4%), ok=True; refresh_feed ran; build 2 reported 19 priors, novel 0, ok=False, identical sha256 a0f3ed4b.... The only thing that changed between the two runs was the staged copy.
entries.disposition: fixed - find_priors now skips any path whose basename equals the excluded candidate's basename, not only the identical resolved path. tests/test_gates.py::test_find_priors_never_returns_a_copy_of_the_candidate pins it. The shipped file's true verdict is the build-1 one: 18 priors, 64.4% novel, 1,048,807 prior px deliberately dropped.

entries.title: gates.find_priors swept the competition inputs in as prior submissions
entries.status: fixed on main (merged), test in tests/test_gates.py
entries.what_it_is: find_priors walked roots that contained training_features.tif, the external USGS/DOE layers and sample_submission.tif, and counted them as prior submissions. The 'prior union' then covered more pixels than the footprint itself, which silently destroys both the novelty fraction and the not-the-union test; in the H54 build it emptied the novel pool to 93 px.
entries.how_we_know: Measured before the exclusion: prior union 5,363,764 px against a 5,167,373 px footprint. Recorded in the comment above the exclusion in src/gems52/gates.py.

entries.title: check_site.py's success line asserted a gate state it never read
entries.what_it_is: The closing print of scripts/check_site.py ended with the fixed sentence 'Scientific slot gate remains closed.' That is a claim about docs/data/submission.json:approved_for_weekly_slot which the script never opened. It was true while every artefact in submission/ was research-only, and became actively false the moment the H55 artefact shipped with approved_for_weekly_slot=True -- so the repo's own publication checker was printing a contradiction of the record it had just validated, in its success message.
entries.how_we_know: grep -n 'Scientific slot gate' scripts/check_site.py -> one hit, inside a literal print, with no read of submission.json anywhere in the function. Observed live: the script exited 0 with 'gate remains closed' while docs/data/submission.json said approved_for_weekly_slot=True and docs/data/feed.json said scientific_gate=True.
entries.disposition: fixed - the sentence is now derived from the record, and has an explicit branch for 'not recorded', because a checker that guesses the state it did not read is worse than one that says it does not know. Same shape as IR-52-007 and IR-52-026: the apparatus that verifies the artefact had an unverified assumption in it.
disclosed
entries.title: The organiser's band-6 tag is contradicted by the survey contractor's own read-me: band 6 is radiometric total count, and the competition grid is node-aligned to the survey grid
entries.what_it_is: Band 6 of data/training_features.tif is tagged data_category = magnetic_data, 'Tilt angle or total curvature - magnetic field derivative for edge detection'. The GeoDAWN contractor read-me (NV5 / EDCON-PRJ, December 2022, Task Order 140G0221F0024) lists tc_raw and tccorr under Radiometrics and contains no tilt-angle channel anywhere in its channel inventory, so the tag does not correspond to any product the survey delivered. The same document gives the survey's Area 2 origin as 243200.0 / 4135400.0 at 100 m spacing, which is node-aligned to the competition grid rather than pixel-aligned.
entries.how_we_know: Two independent lines. First, the contractor read-me's own channel inventory. Second, measured on the bytes: Spearman(band 6, GeoDAWN total-count grid) = +1.0000; Spearman(band 6, K+Th+U) = +0.9915, which is what a total-count channel is by construction; and |Spearman| <= 0.148 against all five magnetic bands in the same file. Band 6 is also strictly positive (range 2.953 to 88.573), where a tilt angle is bounded by +/-pi/2. Independently corroborated by IR-52-019.
entries.handling: Band 6 is assigned to View B (as B_band6_TC), not to the potential-field view. A radiometric band inside View A would corrupt the conditional-independence test the two views are required to pass. Enforced by tests/test_r4.py::test_band6_is_in_view_b.
entries.evidence: evidence/h53_band6_identity.json and the GeoDAWN read-me, both of which were in data/external/audit_sources/ when first recorded
entries.provenance_warning: This entry was reconstructed on 2026-10-08 after the workspace reset (IR-R4-001) destroyed data/external/audit_sources/GeoDAWN_ReadMe.pdf together with the uncommitted register entry. The measured half (the Spearman evidence and the positivity argument) is reproducible from committed code; the documentary half rests on the session record and should be re-verified against a re-fetched copy of the read-me before being relied on.

entries.title: The two-view co-training arm is refuted by its own pre-registered test (credited-core alternate round)
entries.what_it_is: H57-2 proposed a Blum & Mitchell two-view co-training emission. Its frozen validation (independence Spearman < 0.6 to proceed) returned Spearman 0.637 / Pearson 0.706 on 33 spatial blocks, and the joint model's top-5000 catalogue density (0.0236) did not beat the View-B single view (0.0244). The arm is ABANDONED as a scored candidate.
entries.how_we_know: evidence/gems57_validate.json (scripts/build_h57_cotrain.py --stage validate, exit 0); density and independence blocks recorded there; scripts/build_h57_emit.py carries the same disclosure in every artifact it writes.
entries.disposition: Not promoted. `--stage cotrain` / `--stage build` were deliberately never run. work/cache/gridscore_joint.npy is reused ONLY as ranker material for the H57 novel arm; the shipped metric bracket credits it with no validated gain, and the site/README/LATEST.txt state the refutation next to the download button.

entries.title: The prior family's per-cell credit allocation is under-determined; only an interval is knowable (credited-core alternate round)
entries.what_it_is: Thirteen owner-reported scores plus the |G| = 14,088.7 px anchor identify the family's total credit but not its per-cell allocation: 574 coverage patterns vs 13 equations. A linear program gives the honest interval for the 25,517-cell credited core: [4,079.1, 5,249.2] px of credit (0.5 % slack on the 4-decimal reported scores). Adding 'more detectors agreeing implies not-less credit' makes the system INFEASIBLE — the reported scores contradict that monotone-consensus model.
entries.how_we_know: evidence/gems57_credit_lp2.json, evidence/gems57_credit_robust.json, work/credit_lp.py (the coarser coverage-count model is also infeasible, same reason); scipy HiGHS linprog.
entries.disposition: Every projection in the README/site/knowledge is published as a bracket (0.227-0.336 for the shipped file), not as a point forecast. The pair identity T(ref) = T(d2-8) = 5,223.13 is still exact and is what pins the anchor.

entries.title: The round-1 private truth is NOT the public labels — both public proxies mis-rank the family (credited-core alternate round)
entries.what_it_is: If the round-1 hidden truth were labels.tif, the 0.2778 champion (whose cells are all >=2.83 px from every label pixel by design) would project to DTI 0.0049 against it, and h28 (reported 0.1839, the weakest of the family) would project to 0.1984, the strongest. Both orderings are contradicted by the actual report. Likewise the uncatalogued-SGMC proxy has no rank correlation with the reported scores (Spearman 0.193, p = 0.53).
entries.how_we_know: work/emit_decision.py -> evidence/gems57_emit_decision.json (exact metric on candidate layouts); evidence/gems57_instrument_validation.json (13 paired proxy/score rows).
entries.disposition: Neither public proxy may select or rank a candidate. Selection this session therefore rested on (a) the reported-score inversion, (b) the containment lattice, and (c) the frozen two-view gates — with the residual uncertainty published as a bracket.

entries.title: scripts/check_site.py could not run to completion at its previous HEAD (local import shadowing) — credited-core alternate round
entries.what_it_is: check_site.py imported hashlib at module level and then re-imported it inside main() three times, which makes hashlib a local name for the whole function: the first use raised UnboundLocalError and the script aborted before running any later invariant, including the H57 ones.
entries.how_we_know: python scripts/check_site.py on the pre-merge tree -> UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'hashlib' where it is not associated with a value; the three inner imports are visible in that revision of the file.
entries.disposition: Inner imports removed in the credited-core alternate branch; the repaired checker runs to completion here and its H57-creditcore block verifies the alternate's bytes, gates, disclosure text and non-pointer status.

entries.title: Three instrument defects produced confident wrong answers before they were caught
entries.observation: (1) Layers.matrix reshaped a layer-major memmap into a (layers*rows, cols) matrix; scikit-learn accepted it and reported 3,292 features instead of 39. (2) make_folds buffered on the component fold id, which is -1 off-catalogue, marking the whole grid as boundary and leaving 0 catalogue pixels in training on every fold. (3) The arm's legal set ANDed the catalogue visibility mask into the grid, restricting every arm to still-mapped faults; all arms then scored exactly 0.0000.
entries.handling: All three fixed in src/gems52/h57.py with a regression test for each the axis convention in particular, which had none.

entries.title: Tracked core rasters differ materially from manifest-pinned owner mirrors; the sample copy also contradicts the official description
entries.what_it_is: The tracked training, label, and sample rasters differ materially from the manifest-pinned owner-mirror copies in decoded pixel content, while their grid profiles match. The staged sample has ones on the staged labels, contrary to the official page's 'total fault absence' description.
entries.observation: The 23-file staged owner mirror passes manifest byte/hash verification, but the three tracked core rasters fail those pins and differ by decoded pixels despite identical grid metadata. training_features.tif has 97,207,447/233,304,040 decoded value mismatches (97,120,016 where both are valid; 87,431 validity-mask mismatches). labels.tif differs at 120,650 pixels despite equal class counts; positive masks intersect at only 663 pixels. sample_submission.tif differs at 60,988 cells: the staged mirror has ones exactly on the staged labels, contrary to the official page description of a sample predicting total fault absence.
entries.how_we_know: Streaming Rasterio pixelwise comparison of data/{training_features,labels,sample_submission}.tif and work/h58_pinned copies; byte/SHA and decoded mismatch counts are recorded in evidence/h58_preflight_integrity.json. The staging restore receipt records all 23 manifest pins passing.
entries.handling: Do not overwrite tracked TIFFs. The H58 runner read the separate work/h58_pinned data root and recorded hashes. The sample was used only for grid profile/finite domain, never for its pixel values. H58 refit View A, View B, and the union on the same staged bytes and folds; it did not reuse the old H57 result, whose input-hash linkage is absent. The H58 promotion gate still failed on severe support shortfall (IR-H58-002). Owner-mirror pin integrity is not organizer authentication.
entries.unverifiable: Which of the two pixel-level raster versions is the organizer-authentic competition input cannot be established from the staged GitHub mirror or the current tracked files. The raw official competition download is login-walled; the sample semantic conflict also remains unresolved.
entries.status: open - critical provenance issue; blocks any upload approval
entries.disposition: Use the staged files only for a clearly labelled owner-mirror research run. No weekly slot is authorized until organizer provenance/label alignment is resolved, even if a local holdout result is positive. Previous H57 scores are historical and not a pinned-data baseline until rerun.

entries.title: The registered H58-A emitter produced a severe F_geo support shortfall
entries.observation: The frozen field has 123,173 positive-support pixels, but the output contains only 22 of the requested 37,654 cells (shortfall 37,632). Every primary hide and block fold is budget-incomparable; the local gate is false. The recorded negative mean lifts are not comparable-budget estimates and must not be treated as evidence against the geological hypothesis.
entries.how_we_know: evidence/h58_result.json and evidence/h58_holdout.json; the exact run source is bound by the code hashes in the result and was committed at b475f46. src/gems52/h57.py applies a 5-pixel square local-maximum filter before the 3-pixel Euclidean greedy exclusion. On the smooth radial F_geo field this leaves essentially site peaks, explaining the sparse output.
entries.handling: No zero-score backfill, threshold change, or post-result rerun was made. The TIFF is retained as a decoded-pattern-unique research artifact only; submission/LATEST.txt remains on H57 and no weekly slot was used. Any corrected emitter requires a fresh registration and a new complete run; it cannot replace this failed result.
entries.status: open — registered local gate failed on support capacity; no promotion
entries.disposition: Report the run as under-budget and non-comparable. Do not interpret its mean DTI deficit as a matched-budget refutation. Resolve by a separately preregistered, code-reviewed follow-up; do not alter the frozen H58 result.

entries.what_it_is: The pseudo-AUC proxy-negative mask used cross-connected raster dilation rather than the preregistered 500 m Euclidean catalogue clearance.
entries.title: Pseudo-AUC proxy-negative clearance did not implement a 500 m Euclidean exclusion
entries.observation: scripts/run_h58.py built the catalogue clearance with scipy.ndimage.binary_dilation(iterations=5) and its default cross-shaped connectivity. Pixels such as offset (3,3), about 424 m on this grid, remain eligible as proxy negatives despite being inside the preregistered 500 m Euclidean exclusion. The reported pseudo-AUC values therefore do not satisfy the frozen mask exactly.
entries.how_we_know: The run source bound in evidence/h58_result.json; compare the `cat_clearance` construction with `knowledge/19_hypotheses_H58_preregistered.md` and `registry/h58_preregistration.json`, which require at least 500 m from every catalogue pixel.
entries.handling: Treat pseudo-AUC numbers as exploratory and do not use them to support a co-training conclusion. The primary same-fold holdout gate does not use these AUC values and independently failed on budget comparability. No post-result mask edit or rerun was made.
entries.status: open — pseudo-AUC diagnostic mask is nonconforming
entries.disposition: Keep the raw values for audit with this limitation attached. A future diagnostic must use a Euclidean 500 m raster dilation and a newly frozen protocol; it cannot overwrite this run.

entries.title: A second H59 build contaminated its own prior-scan and drifted the arm by 10 px
entries.what_it_is: build_h59_submission.py scans submission/ and docs/downloads/ for aligned priors; after the first build, its own outputs sat in those roots, so run 2 treated run 1's TIFF as prior support (47 -> 50 priors) and emitted a 14,777-px arm instead of 14,787 - the artifact was not a fixed point, which had been the claim made while proving determinism.
entries.how_we_know: Measured live in this session: same saved fields, same seed, different arm; the two stems differed (arm14787px vs arm14777px) while the receipts both said 'deterministic'.
entries.handling: prior_inventory() now excludes any path named gems52-h59* or h59-candidate*; the rebuild was re-run and verified byte-identical (sha256 e884f84a... both times, n_priors back to 47); a regression test (tests/test_h59.py::test_h59_prior_inventory_excludes_its_own_round) pins the self-exclusion.
entries.status: resolved - fixed in the build and covered by a test; the episode is itself the lesson: a prior scan must always exclude the round it is building
entries.disposition: Keep self-exclusion permanent; any future round copying this builder must inherit the filter or repeat the bug.

entries.title: Portal rejection 'Predicted values must be in range [0, 1]' reported by the owner
entries.what_it_is: The owner reported the DrivenData validator rejecting a submission with exactly that message. Every raster this repository ever served as a primary download that could produce it is one carrying non-finite pixels — every comparison against a NaN is False, so a single such pixel trips the range check, and the historical '-nan' alias exports (knowledge/09) plus a research-only NaN-bearing alias previously linked prominently on the site match the error exactly.
entries.how_we_know: Re-read of the served artifacts: the shipped H59/H57/H56 canonical files are all-finite {0,1} (verified from bytes); the demoted alias tif re-reads with NaN outside the footprint; the error string is what the portal returns for both non-finite and out-of-range values.
entries.handling: The site now leads with one-click all-finite artifacts (docs/executive-summary.html), the NaN-bearing alias is demoted and labelled, and gems52.grid.write_geotiff refuses to emit non-finite/out-of-range arrays at the source, with the build's format gate verifying the re-read bytes. If the owner re-submits the exact H59 bytes (sha256 e884f84a...) and STILL sees the range error, that would be new information: this file provably contains only 0.0 and 1.0, so the rejection would then point at transport corruption or the wrong file being uploaded, and the owner-side sha256 check in the ZIP's STATUS.txt is the first diagnostic.
entries.status: mitigated at source - open until an owner upload of the H59 bytes confirms it
entries.disposition: Never ship a primary download that re-reads non-finite; verify the uploaded file's sha256 equals the receipt's before reporting any portal rejection as unexplained.

entries.title: Two concurrent sessions both labelled a round 'H59'; the parallel one moved submission/LATEST.txt without a slot-gate receipt
entries.what_it_is: While this session's H59 co-training round was running (its preflight at 02:2x UTC), a parallel session merged PR #27 with its own H59 (multi-scale edge coherence + A-only boost, gems52-h59-edge-coh-cotrain-37654px-20261008T022050Z-0f0984928454.tif, sha256 4a60f941...) and repointed submission/LATEST.txt at it. Its receipt records format checks and novelty against h33 only (0.988 vs one prior) but no blocked holdout lift, no support-union gate over all priors, and no registered slot bar - the same approval-without-comparable-evidence pattern as IR-57-107. The collision also invalidated this session's determinism claim mid-flight: the prior-count grew from 47 to 49 rasters, so the fixed-point rebuild had to be redone honestly.
entries.how_we_know: git log on main (7c8c9d4 merge of PR #27, commit 9583756 dated 02:26:47Z); the parallel receipt evidence/gems52-h59-edge-coh-cotrain-37654px-20261008T022050Z-0f0984928454.json has no slot-gate fields; docs/data/submission.json on main still described the H57 pointer, so LATEST and the current-round receipt were decoupled by that move.
entries.handling: The merge of main into this branch (1) keeps every parallel-session artifact, page and receipt byte-intact (its TIFFs, h59-method.html, h59-evidence.html and its build script, now preserved verbatim as scripts/build_h59_edgecoh_submission.py); (2) reverts submission/LATEST.txt and docs/submission/LATEST.txt to the H57 pointer, because under the standing rule an artifact without a registered comparable holdout may not be the current pointer; (3) treats the parallel TIFF as a genuine prior: this session's build excluded only its own exact filenames (prefix exclusion would have wrongly hidden a real prior), re-ran against 49 rasters, and re-published (new canonical sha256 e87ee46c... - the honest consequence of a larger prior set, not a drift); (4) publishes disclosure paragraphs on index/executive-summary/downloads.
entries.status: reconciled - both rounds published; pointer discipline restored; future rounds must use unique round labels (adopt: date-prefixed ids) to prevent label collisions
entries.disposition: No upload or weekly slot is approved for EITHER H59 artifact; the parallel round remains downloadable research whose local numbers are format/uniqueness-only. The label collision itself is recorded so neither session's receipts can later be mistaken for the other's.

entries.title: A third concurrent 'H59' (view-B field) reached main moving the LATEST pointer and overwriting the short-path alias
entries.what_it_is: PR #30 (commit 867a2de) published gems52-h59-cotrain-view_B-37654px-20261008T033705Z-54debe0d-zeros.tif, rewrote docs/data/submission.json to describe it as the current round, pointed submission/LATEST.txt at it, and replaced docs/downloads/h59-candidate.zip with its own copy. The artifact itself checks out byte-honest (single-band float32, all finite, {0,1}, 37,654 px, EPSG:32611, 3730x3292 - re-verified during this merge), but its receipt carries no blocked-holdout lift, no all-prior support gate and no registered slot bar, and it reuses this session's scripts/run_h59.py path for a different 816-line program while borrowing this round's registration prose.
entries.how_we_know: git log origin/main (079f0b5 merge of PR #30; 867a2de file list) and the pre-merge submission.json/LATEST.txt contents on main; the run-script divergence measured as 484 insertions / 755 deletions against this session's runner.
entries.handling: Merge resolution on arena/3d4a53e2-gemsdoe52: (1) the view-B TIFF, ZIP, receipt and pages stay in the tree under their own names, and its runner is preserved verbatim as scripts/run_h59_viewb.py with a provenance note; (2) submission/LATEST.txt, docs/data/submission.json and the h59-candidate short paths are restored to this branch's state (H57 pointer; h59-candidate = the union artifact); (3) the pointer revert follows the same standing rule applied in IR-H59-004 and IR-57-107 - a format-valid artifact without a registered comparable holdout cannot be the current pointer; (4) the view-B TIFF is inside this round's 49-raster prior scan, so the canonical union artifact is novel against it by construction (the 03:49Z rebuild predates the merge by minutes - final hashes after this merge re-verified below by re-running the fixed-point build).
entries.status: reconciled - three concurrent rounds all published and labelled; pointer discipline restored; IR-H59-004's unique-label recommendation now has two confirmed collisions behind it
entries.disposition: The view-B round remains downloadable research; no upload or weekly slot approved without a registered holdout. If its owner record can produce one, the gate reopens identically to H59's.

entries.title: The |G| = 14,088.7 anchor is an assumption, not a measurement
entries.what_it_is: knowledge/01 and scripts/h57_common.py both use G_ANCHOR = 14088.7 px of hidden truth. Deriving it requires assuming M = T (emitted hit-mass equals credited mass) for both members of the nested prior pair, on top of assuming the deleted 100-200 m ring carried no hit-mass.

entries.disposition: killed
entries.title: Thirteen public scores cannot localise the hidden truth
entries.what_it_is: The metric linearises in a relaxed truth density, so 13 scores give 13 linear constraints. Under a uniform-truth assumption the implied |G| ranges from 11,349 to 499,618 across the 13 priors, with several priors admitting no solution; allowing the density to vary over 12,051 blocks with box bounds, the equality system is infeasible at every N from 1,000 to 60,000.
entries.how_we_know: work/f3_tomography.py, using W_i = max-convolution and K_i = sum-convolution of each prior with the exact triangular kernel.
entries.handling: Killed. The first-order E[max] ~ sum approximation for M fails exactly where the truth is concentrated, which is where faults are. No further attempt will be made to invert public scores into a truth map.

entries.title: The uniqueness gate compared the artefact against its own canonical download alias

It cannot cover the canonical alias the round's short alias (now docs/downloads/h60-cotrain-candidate.tif), whose basename differs from the artefact's.  Once the alias exists, any later run of the gate counts the artefact as a prior and reports the one verdict that would stop a legitimate submission.

The alias was confirmed byte-identical to submission/<name>.tif by SHA-256 before it was excluded.

Pinned by tests/test_h60.py::test_the_canonical_alias_is_not_counted_as_a_prior, which asserts both the gate verdict and the byte-identity that makes the exclusion legitimate rather than a way of hiding a real duplicate.

entries.disposition: disclosed
entries.title: Two differently-named scored submissions have byte-identical decoded content; the reported score is identical too
entries.what_it_is: data/scored/8GEMSDOE_Hedge-v2_submission.tif (736,494 bytes) and data/scored/gemsdoe-ens12-adopted-7f00890a.tif (570,890 bytes) differ in file size and compression but decode to exactly the same 227,507-pixel emission (|I & J| = 227,507 = |I| = |J|). Both are reported by the owner as 0.1563.
entries.how_we_know: Pixel-set comparison of the two restored rasters on the sample-submission grid; the H60 stage-2 pairwise overlap table.
entries.why_it_matters: It is the only internal consistency check available on the owner-reported file-to-score mapping: two artefacts with identical decoded content were reported with an identical score, so the mapping is at least self-consistent for this pair. It does NOT authenticate the mapping, because the board publishes no filename and both rows could be the same recording of one upload.
entries.handling: Treated as one file ('I', the GEMSDOE8 family) in every twelve-file computation, so the corroboration counts are not double-weighted.
entries.note: Distinct from main's same-numbered entry, which is preserved above under its original id.

entries.disposition: disclosed
entries.title: The twelve scored files are not jointly consistent: file C is a strict subset of file D yet reports a higher score
entries.what_it_is: C = gems24-d1-5 (60,069 px, 0.2477) is a strict subset of D = topo-gap-closure (61,328 px, 0.2449): measured C \ D = 0 px and D \ C = 1,259 px. Under the additive-atom model with M = T this requires the 1,259 extra pixels to carry -3.5 credit units, which is impossible.
entries.how_we_know: Exact set algebra on restored bytes, then T_i = score_i x (0.2 S_i + 0.8 |G|) with |G| = 14,088.7.
entries.why_it_matters: The raw LP is infeasible. A slack of max(4.0, 0.002 T_i) -- the smallest band that makes the system feasible -- is therefore applied to every equation and reported. It widens every identified interval slightly.
entries.handling: Intervals are computed with the slack and the slack size is published alongside them; no interval is reported as if the system were exactly consistent.
entries.note: Distinct from main's same-numbered entry, which is preserved above under its original id.

entries.disposition: disclosed
entries.title: Atom credit is set-identified, not point-identified; every non-file candidate set has a lower bound of zero
entries.what_it_is: Twelve equations in 559 unknown atom credits. Linear programming over the feasible polytope gives P1 = A n C credit in [4,132.6, 5,233.6] but gives A n I (4,814 px), E n I \ A (14,073 px) and cross-family sets a lower bound of exactly 0.
entries.how_we_know: scripts/h60_identify.py, per-set LP min and max with constraints t >= 0, sum t <= |G|, t <= 3|a|.
entries.why_it_matters: Any arm built from the priors has an UNMEASURABLE credit density. Earlier rounds reported NNLS point estimates for these same quantities, which select one corner of the polytope and invent information the organiser's scores do not contain.
entries.handling: Decisions are taken on intervals and the projection is published as a table over the arm-density prior, never as a single forecast.
entries.note: Distinct from main's same-numbered entry, which is preserved above under its original id.

entries.disposition: refuted
entries.title: The preregistered corroboration-ladder model is refuted by the organiser's own scores
entries.what_it_is: A four-coefficient model rho(c, f) = rho_clade * r_clade^(c-1) * r_ext^f fitted to the twelve measured credits reproduces them with median |relative error| 0.22, maximum 0.83, and leave-one-file-out median 0.28; file M is missed by a factor of 11 out of sample.
entries.how_we_know: scripts/h60_ladder.py, weighted least squares with 12 random restarts, plus a leave-one-file-out refit.
entries.why_it_matters: Corroboration count is not a sufficient statistic for credit density -- the same conclusion knowledge/03 N-10 reached by a different route ('habitat is not credit'). No arm may be sized on a corroboration-ladder argument.
entries.handling: Recorded as a refutation. The ladder was not used to size or rank the arm.
entries.note: Distinct from main's same-numbered entry, which is preserved above under its original id.

entries.disposition: disclosed
entries.title: |G| rests on a single nested pair, and publication rounding moves it by +/-70 px
entries.what_it_is: |G| = 14,088.7 px is solved from the single exact relation A subset B with the B \ A ring (6,436 px) carrying zero credit. Varying the two reported scores by one unit in the fourth decimal moves |G| by about 70 px.
entries.how_we_know: Analytic propagation: G = (score_B * 8818 - score_A * 7530.8) / (0.8 (score_A - score_B)).
entries.why_it_matters: Every credit and every density in the round scales with |G|. There is no second nested cross-family pair available to check it.
entries.handling: |G| is quoted to one decimal with the rounding band stated.
entries.note: Distinct from main's same-numbered entry, which is preserved above under its original id.

entries.disposition: fixed
entries.title: The out-of-fold fold assignment covered only catalogue pixels, so the independence test had zero blocks
entries.what_it_is: The first H60 co-training run assigned folds from connected components of the label raster only, leaving every non-catalogue pixel with fold 0. Out-of-fold probabilities were therefore undefined on exactly the labelled negatives the independence test needs, and the test reported blocks=0, rho=nan.
entries.how_we_know: Run log: 'blocks=0  rho=nan'.
entries.why_it_matters: A nan independence statistic would have been reported as 'premise not refuted', which is the wrong answer for the right-looking reason.
entries.handling: Folds are now a 200 px tile partition over the whole grid, assigned by (i + 2j) mod 4 so every 4-neighbour tile is in a different fold, with catalogue components forced whole into the fold of the tile holding their centroid.
entries.note: Distinct from main's same-numbered entry, which is preserved above under its original id.

entries.disposition: fixed
entries.title: The hide-and-recover survival check contradicted itself, and the first fold assignment emptied the training positives
entries.what_it_is: Two defects in the same block of code. (a) The training buffer was built from the training positives themselves (dilation of lab on the non-held folds), so 'lab and not buffer' was empty and clf.fit raised on a (0, 20) array. (b) The survival statistic divided the held-out truth by a buffer that by construction contained it, so survival always printed 0.000 while the emission set was in fact unrestricted.
entries.how_we_know: Run logs for both defects; the fix is the R4 section 4 rule that the held-out segment must be removed from the catalogue that builds the exclusion and must remain inside the placeable set.
entries.why_it_matters: (b) is the dangerous one: a printed survival of 0.000 would have invalidated every hide-and-recover number in the round while looking like a real result.
entries.handling: Buffer = dilation of the held-out fold only; survival = fraction of the held-out truth that lies inside the placeable candidate set.
entries.note: Distinct from main's same-numbered entry, which is preserved above under its original id.

entries.title: The round's self-exclusion pattern missed the stem-named docs/downloads copy of its own artifact, so the second E3 build treated its own previous arm as a prior and the lane gate fired on it at 90.4% within-3px (a self-collision, not lane drift)
entries.what_it_is: prior_inventory excluded only the portal name `gems52-h60-<field>-arm<N>px-<hash8>-zeros.tif` and the short-path copies. The canonical stem-named copy `gems52-h60-dis_contrast-arm37654px.tif` in docs/downloads (written by the first build) entered the prior scan as a 56th prior; the rebuild then excluded its own previous arm's support from the pool, forcing the new dots into the 1-3 px ring around the old dots, and the lane gate read 0.9038 within-3px against it — a false duplicate alarm against the round's own previous build (the H59 IR-H59-001 fixed-point problem in a new guise).
entries.how_we_know: The second build logged 'prior support union: 1403610 px from 56 aligned rasters' (vs 55 in the first build) and the lane gate's worst prior was docs/downloads/gems52-h60-dis_contrast-arm37654px.tif at 0.9038; the artifact sha256 changed between builds (501fd364... then 4bb60f42...).
entries.fix: The self-exclusion regex now covers BOTH published names of the round's own artifact (stem and -zeros portal name) plus the short-path copies; all H60 outputs were cleaned and the build re-run to the fixed point (55 external priors, deterministic artifact sha256 0add72cd69542f19...). The lane gate no longer sees the round's own outputs, exactly as the H59 self-exclusion principle intends; parallel sessions' same-round artifacts remain genuine priors.

entries.title: The preregistered greedy_emit coverage placement selects the disagreement field's broad-plateau mass, which on the required-novel pool is anti-correlated with the holdout truth (hide pooled 2.6e-05, ~50x below the matched novel-pool random control)
entries.what_it_is: greedy_emit maximizes triangular-kernel coverage of the density field. For dis_contrast on the novel pool (footprint & ~200 m ring & outside all prior support) the gain favours broad moderate plateaus (mean field at greedy dots 0.349) over thin high crests, and that plateau mass is anti-correlated with the withheld catalogue truth: the greedy-placed 37,654-px arm scores hide-instrument pooled HOLDOUT-DTI 2.6e-05 (fold-mean), while the same field placed by the registered scoring emitter (h57.iso_select top-k) scores 3.5e-03, above the matched novel-pool random control (1.4e-03), consistent with the registered field read (0.004109 pooled on the full legal pool). A greedy-placed raster would therefore NOT externalize the measured field.
entries.how_we_know: Placement diagnostic in the E3 build: greedy and iso emissions of the same field on the same pool overlap in only 838 of 37,654 px; both were scored on the same 4 hide + 4 tip folds; the greedy diagnostic is retained in evidence/h60_build.json (greedy_diagnostic.holdout) and the run card.
entries.fix: Registered correction H60-5: the shipped artifact is placed by the registered SCORING emitter h57.iso_select (top-k, min_px 3.0 inclusive, nms_px 5, budget 37,654) — the emitter of every registered read and of the H57 champion artifact. greedy_emit is retained as a disclosed, scored diagnostic. No gate outcome changes: the promotion rule had already failed on the registered reads and the verdict stays negative.

entries.title: The lane-drift 3-px proximity gate fired at 0.8392 against an owner-supplied CALIBRATION lattice (bar 0.70) — a geometric false positive, not lane drift

The reading measures grid geometry, not duplication of another lane's discovery.

Raw readings are still reported per prior; BOTH Spearman components apply to every prior without exception; the uniqueness gate (the actual duplication control) is unchanged and passes decisively (pattern unique, novelty 100% vs all 55 priors). entries.status: corrected in the shared forensic instrument; historical |G| superseded
entries.title: The published |G| = 14,088.7 px lies outside the rigorous identification interval
entries.what_it_is: Thirteen owner-reported scores give thirteen equations in fourteen unknowns (13 credits plus |G|), so |G| is only set-identified. Two rigorous constraint families bound it: T_i <= |G| for every file, and max-cover monotonicity T_X <= T_Y on every measured nested pair. On the restored bytes with masked support the interval is [5,949.3, 12,512.1] px. The point value 14,088.7 published by H60 and used for its marginal bar, credit densities and LP is above the upper bound.
entries.how_we_know: scripts/h61_forensics.py -> evidence/h61_forensics.json (G_identification.masked, subset_pairs, G_point_under_zero_ring_credit.sensitivity_to_ring_credit). Binding lower file calib_8GEMSDOE_Hedge-v2_submission; binding nested pair scored_d15_scored (0.2477, 60,069 px) subset of scored_gems27_tgc_v2_d15 (0.2449, 61,328 px).
entries.handling: All H61 economics are reported at both interval ends. 14,088.7 is retained only as the value implied by the extra, unproven assumption that the 6,436 px the champion deleted earn exactly zero credit; the sensitivity table shows 25 credit of ring income moves it to 12,333 px.
entries.disposition: Do not reuse 14,088.7 as a measurement. Any promotion arithmetic must carry the interval.

entries.title: The literal 3 px lane rule is unsatisfiable on a registry containing a universal-coverage probe
entries.what_it_is: The 13GEMSDOE spacing-five lattice's 3 px halo covers 1.0000 of the eligible footprint (a spacing-5 square lattice has maximum interior distance sqrt(8) = 2.83 px), so every nonempty raster has 100% of its dots within 3 px of that one prior and the literal rule returns DUPLICATE for all of them. CTD5 stopped on exactly this.
entries.how_we_know: gems52.gates.registry_coverage measured this session: lattice coverage 1.0000 (probe), champion h33-2-b2 coverage 0.1514 (informative), h19-5 0.1915, d1-5 0.1765. Re-measured on the restored census: CTD5's informative-prior near-dot fractions are 0.1063-0.1368 with |rho| <= 0.0046, i.e. its STOP was caused entirely by the probe.
entries.handling: gems52.gates.lane_report classifies a prior with measured 3 px coverage >= 0.95 as a universal-coverage probe, applies the literal 0.70/3 px and 0.90 rank rules to informative priors, and still reports the literal statistic for every prior including probes. Nothing is deleted and no threshold is relaxed.
entries.disposition: Policy is a property of the prior, measured, uniform and prospective; it is not a per-round exception.

entries.status: measured; explains four previous failed disagreement arms
entries.title: View A (potential field / subsurface) does not transfer between spatial quadrants
entries.what_it_is: Under the corrected label-blind-quadrants-v2 splitter, View A's out-of-fold AUC on a held-out quadrant is 0.5062, 0.6011, 0.4668 and 0.4910 (mean 0.5163) while its in-sample AUC on the training quadrant is 0.9135-0.9481. View B (DEM curvature/slope plus band 6 and the external K, Th, U, Th/K, U/K, U/Th) reaches 0.6625, 0.7684, 0.6112 and 0.6952 (mean 0.6843). A view that fits its own quadrant and predicts chance in the next one is not a sufficient view, so the Blum-Mitchell premise fails and there is no information for A to hand B.
entries.how_we_know: evidence/h61_fit_checkpoint.json (per-fold in-sample and held-out region AUC), evidence/h61_canary.json (max single-feature held-out AUC 0.6687, alarm 0.90, no alarm).
entries.handling: Reported as the round's primary negative result. The exchange was still executed exactly as preregistered and the disagreement arm still evaluated at matched budget, so the falsification is at the registered operating point rather than assumed.
entries.disposition: Any future co-training round must first show View A transfer above chance, or change what View A is (for example a physically forward-modelled basement-depth step rather than raw potential-field channels).

entries.status: measured and reported; verdict NOT relaxed; prospective fix recommended to the shared selector
entries.title: The directed 3 px proximity rule has a chance level, and 31 registry rasters sit above its own trigger
entries.what_it_is: The statistic 'fraction of YOUR dots within 3 px of prior P' has chance level equal to P's own 3 px coverage of the eligible footprint: a uniformly random emission lands inside P's halo with exactly that probability. The rule's trigger is 0.70, so for any prior whose coverage is at or above 0.70 the rule fires on a random emission and cannot indicate lane drift. Measured over the 545-raster registry: 14 rasters have coverage >= 0.95 (probes under the preregistered policy) and 31 have coverage >= 0.70; of the 23 near-offenders, 14 are probes and all 9 informative ones have coverage 0.7583-0.8976 with NEGATIVE excess over chance (-0.0054 to -0.0291). Across all 545 priors the median excess is -0.0766 and only 108 are positive, i.e. the H61 emission is less clustered near prior dots than uniform chance. Max Spearman is 0.0361 (literal) / 0.0209 (policy) against a 0.90 trigger.
entries.how_we_know: scripts/h61_lane_analysis.py over evidence/h61_lane_dots.json (gems52.gates.lane_report on the written artefact, 545 rasters, 361 distinct decoded patterns), which itself measured per-prior coverage with gems52.gates.registry_coverage.
entries.handling: The preregistered probe threshold (0.95) and the literal 0.70/3 px rule were NOT relaxed: the recorded verdict stays DUPLICATE/STOP and the artefact stays research-only. The chance-normalised excess is published beside it so the reader can see that the STOP is a property of the registry's geometry, not evidence of a copied lane.
entries.disposition: Prospective fix for the shared selector, to adopt BEFORE the next round: apply the directed proximity rule only to priors whose measured coverage is below the rule's own trigger, or test the chance-normalised excess (near - coverage) against a margin. Both forms follow from the rule rather than being tuned to a result.

entries.title: The two footprints are not nested: 1,540 training-footprint pixels are not in the submission domain and 3,073 submission-domain pixels are not in the training footprint
entries.what_it_is: The all-19-band finite footprint of data/training_features.tif (5,165,840 px) and the finite domain of data/sample_submission.tif (5,167,373 px) are NOT nested in either direction: 1,540 px are finite in every competition band but not finite in the sample, and 3,073 px are finite in the sample but not in every band. Their intersection is 5,164,300 px. Every earlier round in this repository computed features on the all-19-band footprint and then handed the emission to submission_writer with the sample domain as the footprint, which raises 'invalid footprint or positive mass outside footprint' the moment a selected pixel falls in the 1,540-px gap.
entries.how_we_know: Measured in this session on the manifest-pinned bytes (scripts/build_h62_submission.py start-up log line 'footprint: all-19-band 5,165,840 px, sample domain 5,167,373 px, intersection 5,164,300 px'). The build failed with that exact ValueError on the first run before the fix; see the IR-H62-001 marker in scripts/build_h62_submission.py.
entries.disposition: The emission domain is now the intersection of the two masks, used both as the candidate pool and as the footprint handed to the validator. The gap is 0.03 % of the grid, so no earlier measured number changes materially, but any future round that emits on the raw training footprint will hit the same fail-closed error.

entries.title: The corroboration operator is structurally unable to fill a usable budget
entries.what_it_is: Two independent thinnings of k dots inside a pool of n intersect in k^2/n dots. At k = 30,000 and n = 4,861,502 that is 185 px even under perfect independence, and at the preregistered q_conf = 0.60 with k = 60,000 the measured intersection is 92 px (View A's confident set thins to 6,307 dots against View B's 31,083). The hard intersection therefore cannot be an emission at any budget this competition scores; conc_corrob's grid is 92 positive pixels and every larger emission from it is zero-field fill.
entries.how_we_know: evidence/h62_cotrain.json -> corroboration_probe; evidence/h62_validation.json -> conc_corrob row (Instrument-2 lift 0.97-0.99x, i.e. indistinguishable from the matched random control at every budget).
entries.disposition: Registered as correction H61-1 before the artifact shipped: the operator is delivered as a ranking on the joint confidence min(pA,pB), and the hard intersection is published as the measured structural negative. Do not attempt to rescue it by lowering q_conf - the k^2/n ceiling is what binds.

entries.title: The two instruments disagree in sign on which field is best, and neither is a board proxy
entries.status: open - irreducible with the data available
entries.what_it_is: On the registered hide-and-recover instrument (HOLDOUT-DTI) the ranking is view_A 0.010332 > conc_soft 0.008467 > clf_union 0.008390 > view_B 0.007970. On the revealed-preference instrument the ranking is view_B 2.67x > clf_union 2.60x > conc_soft 1.42x > view_A 1.08x random. The two orderings are almost inverses. The first instrument is known to be uninformative about the board (Spearman(owner-reported, simulated) = -0.1045, n = 13; the 0.2778 champion ranks 13/13 on it); the second is a similarity statistic to one specific prior file.
entries.how_we_know: evidence/h62_validation.json, both instrument tables, computed this session on the manifest-pinned bytes with the evaluator modules pinned by SHA-256.
entries.disposition: Both orderings are published side by side and neither is presented as a leaderboard forecast. The shipped field is chosen by the preregistered rule (highest revealed-preference lift among fields that are not merely the union), and the register's verdict 'promote' is explicitly scoped to the registered instrument only. Resolving the conflict needs an organizer-authenticated label set, which this sandbox cannot obtain.

entries.title: The lane-drift 3 px proximity component uses a 25-cell L1 diamond, not the metric's 29-cell Euclidean disc
entries.what_it_is: h60d.lane_drift_report measures 'dots within 3 px' with scipy.ndimage.binary_dilation(prior_dots, iterations=3), whose default structure is the 4-connected cross. Three iterations therefore produce the 25-cell L1 diamond, whereas the competition metric's kernel k(d) = max(1 - d/R, 0) with R = 3 px covers the 29-cell Euclidean disc. Every near-dot fraction this repository has reported is consequently a LOWER bound on the fraction of dots within the metric's own 300 m acceptance radius.
entries.how_we_know: Measured: the dilation of a single pixel on a 20x20 grid covers 25 of 400 cells, not 29; pinned by tests/test_h62.py::test_revealed_colocation_matches_a_hand_computation. The metric's disc is enumerated by gems52.metric._offsets (29 offsets at |offset| <= 3 px).
entries.disposition: Disclosed rather than silently widened: changing the structure now would make every prior round's proximity number unverifiable, and the reading is conservative in the direction that matters (a run that passes at 0.2781 on the diamond would read higher on the disc, so the gate is not being made easier to pass without saying so). H61's worst gate value is 0.2781 against a 0.70 bar, so theconclusion does not change under the wider disc.

entries.title: This round preregistered its emission budget on a |G| bracket that is disjoint from the measured one
entries.status: open - disclosed as correction H62-4; the emission was not changed
entries.what_it_is: registry/h62_preregistration.json derives the 22,000 px emission budget from the champion-family decay gamma = 0.2284 evaluated over a |G| bracket of 18,000-19,300 px, which yields S* = 21,300-22,870 px. That bracket is DISJOINT from the interval |G| is actually identified to live in. |G| is bounded below by T <= |G| applied to the largest off-catalogue support (calib_8GEMSDOE_Hedge-v2, 166,519 px at score 0.1563 -> |G| >= 5,949.3 px) and above by monotone credit on the tightest nested scored pair (d15 60,069 px subset gems27_tgc_v2_d15 61,328 px, 0.2477 > 0.2449 -> |G| <= 12,512.1 px). The legacy point |G| = 14,088.7 px used by knowledge/10 and carried into this round is a valid but NON-BINDING upper bound (it comes from the weaker nested pair h33-2-b2 subset d28); treating it as a point value additionally assumes the champion's 6,436 deleted ring pixels earn exactly zero credit, and it falls to 7,066 px if they earn 100 px.
entries.how_we_know: Independently re-derived in this checkout: the subset relation d15 subset gems27 and the 166,519 px off-catalogue support were recomputed from the manifest-pinned bytes directly, and both bounds reproduce evidence/h61_forensics.json (main's H61) to four decimal places. The nested-pair algebra is G <= 0.25*(s_y*S_y - s_x*S_x)/(s_x - s_y) from DTI = T/(0.2 S + 0.8|G|) with T monotone in support; the lower-bound algebra is G >= 0.2*s*S/(1 - 0.8*s) from T <= |G|. Recorded in the build receipt as g_bracket_px and g_sensitivity.
entries.disposition: Disclosed as correction H62-4 rather than silently re-emitting. Under the measured bracket the two available gamma rules disagree: this round's own gamma = 0.6453 clamps S* to 30,000 px at every |G| in the bracket, while the champion-family gamma = 0.2284 gives S* = 7,044-14,815 px and clamps to 15,000 px. The direct board measurement - score strictly decreasing in emitted mass across the six off-catalogue scored priors (Spearman -1.000, n = 6) - breaks the tie toward the LOW end, so 15,000 px is the value the evidence favours and 22,000 px is above it. The shipped file is left at 22,000 px (the preregistered fallback, which sits between the two model answers) rather than churned a second time after the review; the budget is now the weakest link in this round and is the first item for the next session.

entries.title: H62-1 corridor length estimator under-counted thin lines (caught by test before results)

entries.title: Weak-surface subgroup evaluator held one full-grid mask per segment and was OOM-killed
entries.what_it_is: The preregistered weak-surface subgroup analysis collected every withheld segment as a full 3,730x3,292 boolean array (hundreds of segments -> >1.5 GB) and the validation process was killed by the OOM killer before writing evidence/h62_validation.json; the log ends without a traceback after the tip fold loop.

entries.title: A frozen artifact's zero-copy claims and the lane-proximity gate are both registry-relative: when a concurrent round's files joined the registry mid-merge, the same build emitted 37,626 px instead of 37,627 and the pre-merge freeze's novel fraction fell from 1.0 to 0.9924; the 3 px proximity gate now flags ANY lattice-placed emission as DRIFT
entries.how_we_know: scripts/build_h62_buriedcorr.py re-run after the merge (work cache untouched): log lines 'prior support union: 1529489 px from 80 aligned rasters', 'legal pool: 3684203 px', 'iso_select placed 37654 px ... 1709 on positive-field crests', 'emitted 37626 px; clipped 28', 'format problems: []; pattern_unique=True, novel_frac=1.0000, n_priors=80', 'lane gate on dots: max|rho|=0.0184, raw within-3px 0.9994 (gate excl. calib: 0.9994) -> DRIFT'. gates.uniqueness_report on the frozen 37627 array vs the same 80 priors: pattern_unique=True, novel_fraction=0.9924. Both artifacts' builds are deterministic given their prior sets; selection is a function of the required-novel pool.
entries.invariant_violated: The brief's invariant 'every emitted pixel is outside every prior submission's decoded support' is true of the shipped candidate only relative to the registry it was measured against. It is NOT a stable property of the bytes. Likewise the lane-proximity gate is not a stable property of an emission: it is a property of (emission, registry, geometry rule) and the geometry rule is chance-level on lattice-dense registries (their IR-H62-004: the 3 px component uses a 25-cell L1 diamond, not the metric's 29-cell disc).
entries.likely_cause: Zero-copy emission is defined against a live, growing registry of prior rasters. Any freeze of a registry-relative artifact without a frozen registry snapshot is provisional. The proximity gate was calibrated when few lattice-dense emissions existed; with several of them in the registry its false-positive rate approaches 1 for any new lattice placement.
entries.detected_by: H62-buriedcorr session, merge of the concurrent H61/H62-concordance rounds
entries.source_claim: the brief's zero-copy invariant and the preregistered 3 px proximity gate were stated as artifact properties
entries.our_measurement: both are (artifact, registry) properties; measured drift as above
entries.impact_on_claims: no leaderboard or organizer-confirmed claim is affected (none exists); the artifact's identity changed and is re-certified against the merged registry
entries.relevance_reason: directly changes what bytes the round ships and how its uniqueness claims must be read
entries.how_detected: post-merge rebuild of the frozen pipeline; side-by-side gates.uniqueness_report on both artifacts
entries.suggestion_or_fix: freeze a registry snapshot (list of hashes) with any registry-relative artifact; treat the 3 px proximity component as descriptive-only until its geometry and chance level are corrected (IR-H62-004) or drop it from gating (IR-H61-005)
entries.what_it_is: H62-buriedcorr froze gems52-h62-buriedcorr-37627px.tif (sha 1f25c4fb...) at 2026-10-09T00:55Z and certified it: decoded-pattern-unique vs 71 accessible priors, novel_fraction 1.0, dots proximity 0.0094. A concurrent arena session's H61/H62-concordance/R5 files then merged into the same tree. The required-novel pool excludes every prior's support, so the identical pipeline on the identical work-cache inputs re-emitted 37,626 px (sha 6b494e7d...) with novel_fraction 1.0 vs 80 priors. The frozen 37,627 file re-measured against the merged registry is still pattern-unique but its novel fraction is 0.9924 (~287 px now inside the new priors' supports). Separately, the preregistered 3 px proximity gate (drop if > 0.30, H60-6 exclusion) now reads 0.9994 for ANY lattice-placed emission because the concurrent emissions are lattice-dense over the same eligible area - the same unsatisfiability the sibling round registered as IR-H61-005/IR-H61-009...
entries.disposition: The H62-buriedcorr candidate is the re-measured 37,626 px file (sha 6b494e7d..., novel_fraction 1.0 vs 80 priors). The 37,627 px freeze is kept with a dated sidecar (submission/gems52-h62-buriedcorr-37627px.json) that marks it superseded and records the 0.9924 re-measure; it is not the current candidate. The proximity gate outcome is reported as DRIFT-flagged under the literal preregistered rule with the registry-saturation explanation, not laundered: the artifact's verdict remains NEGATIVE/not-slot-approved regardless. Build scripts now emit dated sidecars so scripts/check_site.py classifies these rasters as later-round (the R5/H61 convention), which keeps earlier rounds' novelty receipts from being silently invalidated. No leaderboard claim changes: no organizer-confirmed score exists for any file.

entries.status: corrected in the results document; the preregistration file itself is frozen and hash-pinned
entries.title: The H63 preregistration overclaimed the persistence term's discrimination of isolated contrasts
entries.what_it_is: knowledge/37 section 2 (H63-A) says the along-tangent persistence 'averages |step| along the local tangent (faults are along-strike continuous; point noise, flight-line artefacts and isolated boulders are not)'. Measured on synthetic fields (tests/test_h63.py): the magnitude column fires on an isolated 5x5 blob as strongly as on a step edge (blob max 0.238 vs edge max 0.159 in the test field), and the persistence ratio of an 8 px-tall edge segment to a long edge is 0.99 vs 1.00 at the tested scales. The term is a contrast-and-continuity feature with weak discrimination at short along-strike scales, not a boulder suppressor.
entries.how_we_know: Direct measurement: h63.step_columns on synthetic plane+edge+blob fields; the assertions are pinned in tests/test_h63.py::test_step_columns_detect_a_synthetic_step_edge.
entries.handling: Recorded and corrected where it is not frozen: knowledge/38 section 4 states the weak discrimination explicitly, and the test docstring pins the honest contract (a contrast detector, not a fault detector). The preregistration document is hash-pinned by registry/h63_preregistration.json, so the correction lives in the results document rather than in a retro-edited protocol.
entries.disposition: Any future round citing the persistence term must cite the measured discrimination limits, not the preregistration's rhetoric.

entries.status: lane-level negative result; recorded as a deliverable
entries.title: Second consecutive View-A sufficiency failure: the co-training lane's A premise has now failed twice
entries.what_it_is: H61 measured a raw-value potential-field View A at mean out-of-fold AUC 0.5163 (in-sample 0.948); H63 measured a step-normalised potential-field View A (38 channels, no raw band values) at 0.5362 on the identical splitter. Both parameterisations are at chance out of quadrant, both far below View B (0.6843 / 0.6862) and below the 0.60 sufficiency bar. Independence held in both rounds (max |rho| 0.1331 / 0.1817), so the failure is sufficiency, not independence. The disagreement arm scored below uniform random in both rounds (H61 0.030584 vs random 0.080426; H63 0.040257 vs random 0.078257).
entries.how_we_know: evidence/h61_fit_checkpoint.json, evidence/h63_fit_checkpoint.json (sufficiency_screen), evidence/h61_holdout.json, evidence/h63_holdout.json (pooled scores and paired differences, 53,186 withheld positives, matched 9,400-dot budgets).
entries.handling: Recorded as a negative deliverable; the H63 artefact is published research-only (DOWNLOAD YES, SUBMIT NO, slots used 0). No re-tuning of either round into a positive result, and no promotion of either artefact. Round label renamed H62 -> H63 after a parallel session's H62 merged to main first (PR #46); the measured numbers are unchanged.
entries.disposition: Do not propose a third View-A parameterisation without new evidence (new data, a different splitter test, or an organiser-authenticated calibration). The lane's own falsification condition has fired twice; the next in-lane candidates are the B-only direction (H63-B) and the credit-localisation analysis (H63-E), both preregistered in knowledge/37 section 2.

entries.status: open - mis-specified operator; not used in H65
entries.title: H60-3 'strike-projected basement step' is a second difference ALONG strike and does not detect a step across the trace
entries.what_it_is: src/gems52/h60.py (build_stack, H60-3 block) computes |d1 + d2 - 2*arr| with d1, d2 shifted along the strike unit vector. A basement step across a strike-parallel trace is constant along the trace, so its along-strike second difference is zero by construction; a ramp is also cancelled. The layers b15_step_nne/nw and b13_step_nne exist in evidence/h60_views.json. registry/h60_preregistration.json (line 18) names them 'H60-3 strike-projected basement steps'.
entries.how_we_know: scripts/h65_operator_audit.py -> evidence/h65_operator_audit.json: synthetic 400x400 px grid, 200 m step across a NNE trace. H60-3 on-trace mean 2.96e-05 vs cross-strike symmetric difference (d=3 px) 1.970 in the same grid units (ratio 1.5e-05). Scratch check: the residual persists with no ramp (2.96e-05 order-1, 2.07e-05 nearest) and vanishes for a pure ramp, so it comes from the discrete step, not from the ramp.
entries.handling: H65 replaces the operator with a cross-strike symmetric difference, regionally detrended. H60 outputs are not edited or withdrawn here; any H60 result that uses b15_step_* as a feature is affected and needs re-running before it is cited.
entries.disposition: Open for review. Check whether any submitted H60 or H60C/H60D artefact used b15_step_* features (evidence/h60_views.json).

A dot of credit k=0.0572 (sqrt(8) px) raises DTI to 0.278208, so it passes the bar alpha*DTI=0.0556 and fails the prose bar 0.0588. entries.invariant_violated: One marginal rule, one formula. The denominator change from adding a dot is alpha (since alpha+beta=1), so the bar is alpha*DTI.

entries.affects: knowledge/01 table (0.32 -> 0.0684 should be 0.0640), knowledge/05 line about the accept-bar; any text quoting 0.068 at 0.32 or 0.0588 at 0.2778.

entries.suggestion_or_fix: Use metric.credit_bar. knowledge/42 carries the corrected statement.

entries.title: Marginal bar: the metric's special case gives α·DTI (0.0556 at 0.2778); the repository's accept_bar gives α·DTI/(1−α·DTI) (0.0588)
entries.what_it_is: Metric identity (ii) in src/gems52/metric.py: an addition helps iff c·(1−α·DTI) > α·DTI·f, with c the credit increment and f the false-positive increment. For one uncovered truth pixel with kernel weight w (f = 1−w) this gives w > α·DTI = 0.0556 at DTI 0.2778. emit.accept_bar(dti) = α·DTI/(1−α·DTI) = 0.0588 is the f = 1 form, which is stricter. README's ≈0.055 is the special case, rounded. An earlier H66 draft called 0.0588 the marginal bar; that draft was wrong.
entries.how_we_know: Algebra from metric identities (i) and (ii), and direct evaluation of emit.accept_bar at DTI 0.2778 (this session).
entries.handling: The README H66 block states both forms with their conditions. No code changed.
entries.disposition: Open, low. Decide in a future round whether emit.accept_bar should use the special-case form; the current form is more conservative than the metric's marginal condition.

entries.title: README 'Why 0.2778 won' writes the DTI denominator as 0.2·(T+S−M)+0.8·(|G|−T); the metric is 0.2·(T+S−M)+0.8·|G|

entries.how_we_know: Algebra: T + α(S−M) + β(|G|−T) = α(T+S−M) + β|G| with α=0.2, β=0.8. The README form is not equal to it.
