entries.status: fixed in this round's runner; template already had the right primitive
entries.title: 3,073 in-domain cells carry the float32 nodata sentinel, which collapses every rank channel
entries.what_it_is: 3,061 cells inside the organiser's domain (labels >= 0) carry -3.4028234663852886e+38 in 18 of the 19 feature bands, and 3,073 in band 6. transform.rank01 bins against lo = min(values), so one sentinel cell makes every rank channel of that band a near-constant: the emitted field becomes noise while the file stays format-valid. This is the failure mode that produces a plausible-looking submission that cannot score.
entries.how_we_know: Direct count over data/training_features.tif against labels.tif, this session; recorded in evidence/h67_preflight.json (in_domain_nodata_sentinel_cells, sentinel_policy).
entries.handling: Use the template's own grid.footprint_from(training_features.tif, bands='all'), which excludes any in-domain cell carrying the sentinel in any band. eligible fell from 5,167,373 to 5,164,300.
entries.disposition: Fixed for H67. Recommended once in the template: any round that ranks raw band values should call grid.footprint_from(bands='all') rather than trusting labels >= 0.

entries.title: Three different cell counts can each be called 'the footprint'
entries.what_it_is: labels >= 0 gives 5,167,373 cells; band-12 non-sentinel gives 5,165,852; the all-19-band intersection gives 5,164,300. Which one is used changes every density, prevalence and credit-per-pixel statistic by up to 0.06 %, and changes whether a candidate's mass is 'inside the footprint'.
entries.how_we_know: evidence/h67_preflight.json cells_domain / cells_feature_finite / eligible.
entries.handling: H67 uses the intersection and states it in every receipt. Cf. IR-52-002.
entries.disposition: Open. The organiser's own definition is not published; the intersection is the only safe one.

entries.title: A blunt 'collapsed channel' guard fails legitimately zero-inflated layers
entries.what_it_is: rank_b10 (distance to earthquake) and grad_b17 (surface conductivity gradient) have more than half the footprint tied at the physical minimum, so their rank-01 range is tiny and a guard of the form 'hi - lo < 0.5 means collapsed' reports a false failure. It fired and stopped the run.

entries.handling: Replaced with a degenerate test that fails only on < 10 distinct rank levels or a raw |value| > 1e30 inside eligible, plus an informational zero-inflation list.
entries.disposition: Fixed. Zero inflation is a property of the data, not a defect.

entries.title: The hide-and-recover budget collapses inside a fold, so it cannot compare concentrated with dispersed fields

Arms stay matched within a fold, but a concentrated emission and a uniform-random emission at 2,134 pixels are not testing the same thing: at that size the pooled DTI is dominated by 0.8*|G_fold| and by how much of the fold the field happens to touch. That page advertised three downloadable H72 candidates, while docs/index.html carried the banner 'Current result: H72 - NEGATIVE STOP. NO H72 TIFF WAS WRITTEN OR PUBLISHED.' Both were on main at the same commit. A visitor could only ever see one of them.
entries.how_we_know: api.github.com pages endpoint (source.branch=main, source.path=/) plus reading both files at HEAD 66dfe7a. buffedlizard55-lab.github.io is not inside the sandbox egress allowlist, so the served bytes could not be fetched directly; the Pages configuration is the authority for which file is served.
entries.impact: The download/submit verdict the brief demands be 'obvious' was ambiguous, and one of the two pages pointed at files the other said did not exist.
entries.disposition: The root index.html is now the single H77 entry point and states one download and one verdict. docs/index.html keeps its own historical banners; the two pages no longer disagree about which round is current.

entries.status: open - disclosed; the re-run receipts are kept because they are what the committed script emits
entries.title: main's committed H61 canary receipt does not match what its own unchanged script produces
entries.what_it_is: scripts/run_h61.py line 212 writes evidence_class = 'LEAKAGE-CANARY AUC (diagnostic, not a DTI score)'. The receipt committed on main at HEAD (evidence/h61_canary.json and its docs/data copy) carries evidence_class = 'HOLDOUT-DTI diagnostic AUC (not a DTI score)'. The script is unmodified in this session, so the committed receipt was either hand-edited or generated before a source change that was committed without regenerating it. Separately, re-running scripts/prepare_data.py reproduces band_inventory.json statistics only to float32 quantisation (e.g. band p99 311.884765625 vs 311.8848876953125), so that receipt is not byte-reproducible either.
entries.how_we_know: git show HEAD:evidence/h61_canary.json compared against a fresh run of `PYTHONPATH=src ./.venv/bin/python scripts/run_h61.py canary` in this session, with git diff --name-only confirming scripts/run_h61.py is unmodified.
entries.impact: The scientific content is unaffected: every AUC in the re-run is bit-identical to the committed value (View A fold 0 heldout_region_auc 0.5062341311661124, in_sample_auc 0.9480777). Only the provenance label and float32 rounding differ. But it means a receipt in this repository can drift from the code that generates it without any test noticing.
entries.disposition: The regenerated receipts are kept, because they are what the committed script actually emits, and the discrepancy is disclosed here rather than hidden by reverting. Recommendation for the next round: add a test that re-runs each generator's emit step against its committed receipt, or pin receipts to the script SHA that produced them.

entries.status: closed - fixed on main by a parallel round's `_created()` dating rule, which supersedes this branch's narrower fix
entries.title: scripts/check_site.py has been reporting a false R5-novelty failure since a parallel round landed an undated raster
entries.what_it_is: check_site.py recomputes R5's decoded-pattern novelty against the rasters it can prove predate R5's build and compares to the receipted 1.0. It now reports 0.992087 != 1.0 and exits with one problem. The classifier `_stamp(q) or built` gives any raster with no parseable YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ stamp in its name or sidecar a stamp of exactly `built`, so `> built` is False and it is judged NOT later and kept in the strict prior set. submission/gems52-h75-dva-variogram-anisotropy-B-37654px-20261009.tif carries the date 20261009 but no T######Z, so it is undated by that rule even though it is a 2026-10-09 round; the docs/downloads/h7{4,5,6}-candidate.tif aliases are undated too, and their bytes differ from their canonical twins so the content-hash expansion does not rescue them.
entries.how_we_know: Measured. (1) Pre-existing: GitHub Actions runs 37985270257 (main 68fc601) and 37982265131 (main 4b122f3) both fail at 'Verify all local website links JSON and download bytes', and locally the check reported 0.992087 != 1.0 with every H77 raster removed. (2) Root cause: `_stamp(q) or built` gave undated rasters a stamp of exactly `built`, so they were judged 'not later'; 76 of 112 swept rasters are undated. (3) This branch's narrower fix reached 1.0000 but over only 9 rasters. (4) main's `_created()` fix reaches 1.0000 over 68 rasters and is the version now on this branch. (5) A separate CI-only failure was also found and fixed here: docs/h77-executive-summary.html linked ../work/h77/board_forensics.json, and work/ is gitignored, so the link resolved locally but was dead in CI's fresh checkout; the receipt is now published at evidence/h77_board_forensics.json.
entries.impact: The site checker exits non-zero on main, so 'check_site.py clean' is no longer a usable pre-merge signal for any round. R5's own artefact and receipt are unaffected: it is still pattern unique and not the prior union over every set tried.
entries.disposition: FIXED, by main rather than by this branch. This branch's first fix excluded undated rasters from the strict prior set; that works but weakens the check badly (strict set fell from 73 to 9 rasters). A parallel round on main fixed the same bug better: `_created(q)` takes the MINIMUM over the earliest receipt recording the content hash, the filename/sidecar stamp and the git add date, so an undated alias inherits its canonical twin's date instead of being dropped, and it added a date-filter-independent duplicate guard against the UNFILTERED prior set. This branch therefore took main's scripts/check_site.py verbatim and dropped its own version. Verified: check_site.py exits 0 and R5 novelty recomputes to exactly 1.0000 over 68 provably-dated rasters -- a far stronger set than this branch's 9.

entries.title: Round-label collision, twice: four sessions ran the same brief in parallel; 'H74', 'H75' and then 'H76' were all merged to main by other sessions first
entries.what_it_is: This round was preregistered, executed, gated and published end-to-end under the label H74. At merge time `gh pr merge 73 --merge` refused with 'not mergeable: the merge commit cannot be cleanly created'. `git fetch origin main` showed a parallel session had already merged its own, scientifically different H74 (directional variogram anisotropy View-B ranker, origin/main 2fc03cd, PR #72) and a third session had taken H75. 30 paths were added by both sides (knowledge/63*, knowledge/64, registry/h74_preregistration.json, scripts/{run,publish}_h74*, evidence/h74_*.json, docs/data/h74_*.json, docs/h74*.html, docs/downloads/h74-*, submission/H74_LATEST.txt) and 7 more were modified by both.
entries.how_we_know: git fetch origin main; git merge-tree / git merge reported the 30 add/add and 7 content conflicts. origin/main's knowledge/63 describes variogram anisotropy, not co-training sufficiency, so the two H74s are different experiments sharing a name.
entries.handling: Identifier-only rename H74 -> H77cond (H77cond was the first free label), the same remedy as IR-H66-015 / commit 9d891a6. Knowledge numbers 63/63a/64 -> 67/67a/68 because main now occupies 63-66. Every rename used `git mv`; no science, no threshold and no measurement changed. CRITICALLY, the preregistration document's BYTES WERE NOT EDITED, so its pinned SHA-256 d117b265d44aed75...e3b55 still validates at its new path knowledge/67_hypotheses_H77cond_preregistered.md and the 'frozen before any fit' claim stays independently checkable -- which is why that frozen document's text still reads 'H74' throughout. The rename is disclosed in registry/h77cond_preregistration.json -> identifier_rename, at the top of knowledge/67a, and in AGENTS.md. The shipped raster was re-issued as gems77cond-line-support-B-cotrain-37654px-20261009T193810Z.tif by a script that ASSERTS the raster SHA-256 is unchanged; it is (49ad6098...f317ad). SECOND COLLISION: while this branch was being integrated, a fourth session merged its own H76 (PR #76, gravity-surface abstention) to main, so the H74->H76 rename collided again and a second identifier-only rename H76 -> H77cond was applied. Labels h53..h76 are now all claimed. Every colliding session has taken the next free INTEGER, so another integer invites a third collision; H77cond follows the repo's existing suffixed-label precedent (h60c, h60d, h65b, h65halo, h66cover, h66cotrain) and shares no path with a plain-h77 session. Knowledge numbers 67/67a/68 are free on main (its numbering stops at 66), so the hash-pinned preregistration did not have to move a second time; its bytes are still untouched and run_h77cond.check_prereg() still prints 'preregistration verified'.
entries.disposition: Process lesson, recorded for the next session: run `git fetch origin main` and check which round labels are already taken BEFORE naming a round, not at merge time. Never edit a hash-pinned preregistration to fix its labels.
entries.measured_effect: Zero effect on any number. Raster SHA-256 identical pre/post rename; `run_h77cond.check_prereg()` re-run after the rename prints 'preregistration verified' for round H77cond; pytest 435 passed / 1 skipped unchanged. Second rename: raster sha256 still 49ad6098...f317ad; pytest unchanged. The rename script's three assertions each caught a real defect: a mistyped expected pin prefix; a path filter anchored to the start of a path segment that skipped knowledge/67_hypotheses_H76_preregistered.md; and a <=140-char note that reached 141 chars because 'H77cond' is four characters longer than 'H76'.

entries.status: resolved - shared tool repaired in place
entries.title: A date-only filename stamp (H75's raster) silently back-dates a later round into every earlier round's build-time prior set, breaking R5's novelty equality check
entries.what_it_is: scripts/check_site.py::check_r5 excludes rasters that post-date R5's build before re-deriving R5's claimed novelty, so a later round cannot retroactively invalidate an earlier receipt. Its _stamp() helper only matched 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS' and 'YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ'. H75 (merged to main from a parallel session) shipped submission/gems52-h75-dva-variogram-anisotropy-B-37654px-20261009.tif -- a date with NO time component -- so _stamp returned None, the file was treated as pre-dating R5, and it plus its docs/downloads/h75-candidate.tif alias entered R5's strict build-time prior set.
entries.how_we_know: check_site.py exited 1 on the merged tree with 'R5 novelty: recomputed 0.992087 != receipt 1.0'. Re-running the exact classification logic standalone listed the strict priors with no parseable stamp; gems52-h75-dva-...-20261009.tif and h75-candidate.tif were the only two entries not present before the merge. This round's own files (gems77cond-...-20261009T193810Z.tif) carry full stamps and were classified correctly as later, so the defect is in the helper's pattern coverage, not in this round's naming.
entries.handling: Repaired in place in scripts/check_site.py (never forked): _stamp() now also accepts a non-digit-delimited YYYYMMDD run, parsed with '%Y%m%d'. strptime rejects impossible dates, and resolving a date-only stamp to 00:00 errs toward counting the file AS a prior, which can only make an earlier receipt harder to satisfy, never easier. After the fix the later-round set is 52 (was 50), R5's strict prior set is back to 71, and R5's recomputed novelty is 1.0000 == the receipt. check_site.py now reports zero problems.
entries.disposition: Open recommendation for future rounds: always put a full UTC timestamp 'YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ' in a shipped raster's filename. The checker is now tolerant, but a date-only name is still ambiguous to the hour.
entries.measured_effect: R5 novel_fraction against its build-time priors 0.992087 -> 1.000000 (receipt value); strict priors 73 -> 71; later-round rasters 50 -> 52; check_site.py exit 1 -> 0. No raster bytes changed.

entries.status: resolved - shared tool repaired in place, and the duplicate guard made dating-independent
entries.title: No filename, receipt or git signal reliably dates a raster, so scripts/check_site.py could not tell a later round's file from an earlier one
entries.what_it_is: check_site.py::check_r5 must exclude rasters that post-date R5's build before re-deriving R5's recorded novelty, otherwise every later round retroactively invalidates an earlier receipt. Three successive oracles each turned out to be unsound in this repository. (1) FILENAME stamps: H75 shipped a date-only name (IR-H77cond-002) and the parallel H76 shipped gems52-h76-gravity-surface-abstention-research-only.tif, which carries no date in the filename at all. (2) RECEIPTS: that round's evidence/h76_run_card.json, evidence/h76_exploratory.json and its submission sidecar contain no generated_utc or any other timestamp field, so there is zero in-repo provenance for when those bytes were made. (3) GIT: this repository's history is bulk/squash-imported, so `git log --diff-filter=A` dates gems52-h54-*, gems52-h59-* and even R5's own raster to the PR #70 merge of 2026-10-09T11:41 -- long after they were produced. `--no-merges` does not change this.
entries.how_we_know: check_site.py exited 1 with 'R5 novelty: recomputed 0.999520 != receipt 1.0'. Instrumenting the exact classification showed the only two overlapping strict priors were submission/gems52-h76-gravity-surface-abstention-research-only.tif and its alias docs/downloads/h76-candidate.tif, 8 pixels each, both with git_add=None and stamp=None. A separate sweep showed the git-dating variant would have excluded 37 priors that overlap R5, including genuinely old h54/h59/h66 files -- the UNSAFE direction, which can mask a real duplicate.
entries.handling: Two changes. (a) _created() now takes the MINIMUM over three signals -- filename/sidecar stamp, the earliest receipt recording that content hash, and the git add date across all refs. Minimum, not maximum, is the safe direction: it can only pull an estimate earlier, which keeps a file IN an earlier round's prior set. Git's error mode here is one-directional (bulk import makes old files look late, never makes new files look old), so inside a min() a spuriously-late git date is harmless. The receipt index is keyed by CONTENT HASH, which is immune to naming conventions, aliases and merge history, and reads each receipt's own generation field rather than the minimum of every date in its text -- taking the text minimum stamped a round's raster with an older round's date and drove R5 to 0.973263. (b) More importantly, the question that could actually hide a problem -- 'are these bytes a duplicate of some other raster?' -- no longer depends on dating at all: canonical_pattern_unique and equals_literal_prior_union are now asserted against the UNFILTERED prior set. A wrong date can therefore only move a historical novel_fraction, never conceal a duplicate.
entries.disposition: Open recommendation for every future round: write a generated_utc into the run card AND a full YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ stamp into the shipped raster's filename. Two sessions in a row shipped neither, and a novelty receipt is only reproducible if its prior set can be reconstructed.
entries.measured_effect: check_site.py exit 1 -> 0. R5 historical novel_fraction 0.999520 -> 1.000000 against 68 build-time rasters (receipt records 71). New dating-independent guard: 125 rasters compared, pattern unique True, identical=[]. No raster bytes changed.

entries.title: H75 writes 0 outside the labelled bounds; the official text says null or nan
entries.what_it_is: The organiser's submission-format text says data outside the bounds is 'null or nan'. The sample_submission.tif uses NaN outside its 5,167,373 finite pixels, and the H75 file writes 0 outside its footprint. This is the same deviation as IR-H73-001. The metric formula treats zero and NaN identically outside bounds, because FPw sums over p(x) > 0 and the kernel maximum is unaffected by zeros. Scored board rows with '-nan' and '-zeros' suffixes both appear on the board.

entries.status: resolved - persistence now verifies by reload
entries.title: Torn writes: 8 of 79 channel .npy files had one 4 KiB page of zeros after the 128-byte header
entries.what_it_is: The first H82 channel build wrote 79 flat eligible-indexed columns with np.save and recorded each file's SHA-256 immediately afterwards. Eight files - exactly the first eight in insertion order, all from the first band processed - did not match their recorded digest. On inspection each had its first 3,968 data bytes zeroed, i.e. the remainder of the first 4 KiB page after the 128-byte .npy header, which corresponds to the first eligible row of the grid (992 pixels of row 36).
entries.how_we_know: Bank.col refused to train and raised 'channel byte-integrity failure: DVA2_det_elev_aniso_l1'. Diagnosed by (a) re-hashing all 79 files against the manifest (8 mismatches), (b) two independent recomputations of the same channel that agreed with each other bit-for-bit and disagreed with the file in exactly 992 pixels, all in row 36, all exactly 0.0, and (c) file mtimes showing a single sequential write pass with no overwrite. The transform is deterministic; the files were not.
entries.handling: Added save_verified() in scripts/run_h82.py: np.save, read the file straight back with mmap_mode='r', require shape/dtype/bit-exact equality (equal_nan=True), and rewrite up to six times before raising. Every np.save in the runner now goes through it - channel columns, fold row indices, per-arm prediction checkpoints, dots, surface, stitched fields and the lane-restricted placement. The rebuild needed 0 rewrites and all 79 digests match.
entries.disposition: Resolved. Recorded in evidence/h82_channels.json as save_verified_by_reload=true, n_channels_needing_rewrite=0, and in the channel manifest as save_attempts_gt1={}. Regression-tested by tests/test_h82.py::test_save_verified_rewrites_a_torn_write, which monkeypatches np.save to reproduce the exact corruption and requires attempts == 2.
entries.measured_effect: No measured number was affected: the guard fired before any model was fitted, so no arm was ever trained on the corrupted columns. Had it not fired, the primary arm would have been fitted on 992 wrong pixels in 8 of 60 channels and the result would have looked legitimate.

entries.status: logged - the frozen primary arm lost, and the reason is attributed
entries.title: The pre-registered primary arm is significantly worse than its own control; the strike-alignment channels are the cause
entries.what_it_is: The frozen primary arm B_DVA2_VSA pooled to HOLDOUT-DTI 0.150591 [0.131262, 0.169201] against single_B 0.174910 [0.152922, 0.196038]; the paired difference is -0.024319 [-0.039025, -0.006869], whose upper bound is below zero. The attribution arms separate the cause: B_DVA2 alone reaches 0.189200 [0.167891, 0.209115] (the best number this repository has measured) while B_VSA alone reaches only 0.142148 [0.124400, 0.159982], below single_B.
entries.how_we_know: evidence/h82_holdout.json, evaluator gems52-pooled-hide-v1, 53,186 withheld positive pixels, 9,400 dots per fold per arm, 1000 paired physical-cluster bootstrap draws; evidence/h82_fit.json out-of-quadrant AUCs show the same ordering in all four folds (B_DVA2 mean 0.7124, single_B 0.6849, B_DVA2_VSA 0.6720, B_VSA 0.6511).
entries.handling: Reported as a negative result. The primary arm was NOT swapped for the better attribution arm, because the frozen preregistration forbids post-hoc promotion of attribution arms (registry/h82_preregistration.json attribution_arms_not_promotable). The raster emitted by E3 is the primary arm's, as pre-registered.
entries.disposition: Logged. Two mechanistic findings are recorded for the next round: (1) theta_max is an argmax over 8 discrete fan directions, so cos(2*delta) against a scalar regional strike takes only 4 distinct values - VSA_cos2reg is a categorical recoding of the winning direction, not a continuous alignment, and its low entropy appears to cost the learner more than it gives; (2) VSA_cos2loc is exactly 0 on 69.9%/53.6%/46.7%/47.8% of eligible pixels by fold, where the local structure tensor is degenerate, so the channel is dominated by a 'no local structure' indicator. A finer fan (16 or 32 directions) and a continuous sub-pixel theta_max are the obvious H77 candidates and must be pre-registered before any fit.
entries.measured_effect: Primary arm loses 0.024319 HOLDOUT-DTI against its control with a 95% CI entirely below zero. Verdict NEGATIVE; 0 slots spent.

entries.status: resolved - repaired in the shared tool, not worked around
entries.title: check_site.py's R5 novelty check was already failing at HEAD: short download aliases look undated, so a later round silently invalidates an earlier round's receipt
entries.what_it_is: scripts/check_site.py re-derives R5's 'novel against every raster the repository has produced' claim instead of trusting it, and excludes rasters whose receipt or filename carries a timestamp LATER than R5's build. Its _stamp() helper looked only at <file>.json and the filename. The short download aliases this repository actually serves (h70/h71/h74/h75-candidate.tif) have neither a matching <alias>.json nor a timestamp in the name, so they were classified as contemporaneous with R5 and folded into R5's prior set. h75-candidate.tif alone moved R5's recomputed novel fraction from the receipted 1.0 to 0.992087 and the script exited with a PROBLEM.
entries.how_we_know: Measured, not inferred: check_site.py on this branch reported 'R5 novelty: recomputed 0.992087 != receipt 1.0'. Moving H82's own aliases out of docs/downloads and re-running reproduced the identical failure, which proves it pre-dates H82. The repo already carries <alias>-receipt.json sidecars for h61/h63/h70/h74 under a name _stamp never looked at, and gems52-h75-...-20261009.tif carries a date but no time, which _stamp's two regexes cannot parse.
entries.handling: _stamp() now also reads the '<stem>-receipt.json' sidecar convention, and falls back to a date-only %Y%m%d match interpreted as 00:00:00 of that day. The fallback is deliberately the strict direction: a same-day round stays contemporaneous and remains in the prior set, so nothing is excluded that could have been present. Backfilled the missing alias receipts (docs/downloads/h71-, h75-, h82-candidate-receipt.json) by copying each canonical submission/<stem>.json whose sha256 matches the alias byte-for-byte; no existing file was edited. publish_h82_site.py now writes the H82 alias receipt on every run so it cannot rot.
entries.disposition: Resolved in the shared tool. After the repair check_site.py reports 'R5 novelty recomputed against 71 rasters: novel fraction 1.0000, pattern unique True' and exits with 0 problems over 88 pages and 365 data files. Future rounds that add a short alias must ship its -receipt.json sidecar, or the alias will look undated again.
entries.measured_effect: R5's recomputed novel fraction returned from 0.992087 to the receipted 1.000000, and the prior set shrank from 73 to 71 rasters (the two aliases that were wrongly counted as contemporaneous). No H82 number changed.

entries.title: The off-catalogue instrument's truth is a proxy for the competition's hidden set, not the hidden set
entries.what_it_is: gems52-offcatalogue-v1 scores recovery of SGMC fault pixels, a different compilation's faults, as a stand-in for G (the faults the USGS/INGENIOUS catalogue lacks). SGMC is compiled from state geologic maps at 1:100k-1:500k, is itself incomplete, and may include non-fault lineaments; the 300 m cut also removes trace extensions by construction even though the organiser has said the new-fault truth includes extensions of mapped traces.
entries.how_we_know: Measured in this round: 70,629 SGMC pixels are off-catalogue at a 0 px cut and 55,562 at a 300 m cut, against 60,988 labels.tif pixels; knowledge/66 already records the 95% disjointness. Amendment 74a added I2b (0 px cut) specifically to bracket the extension question, and the two differ (single_B OFFCAT-DTI 0.107456 vs 0.090632).
entries.handling: I2 and I2b are reported as OFFCAT-DTI, never as HOLDOUT-DTI and never as a board forecast. registry/h83_preregistration.json states that a second instrument can demote but never promote; the verdict is decided only by gems52-pooled-hide-v1.
entries.disposition: Recorded as a limit of the instrument, not a defect of the run. Both numbers are published.
entries.measured_effect: I2 single_B vs random: 0.090632 vs 0.083641 (lift +0.0070). I2b: 0.107456 vs 0.073864 (lift +0.0336). I1: 0.174571 vs 0.080426 (lift +0.0941). The surface detector's skill collapses on the off-catalogue population.

entries.title: The full-census literal dots rule is unsatisfiable for every non-empty raster
entries.what_it_is: The lane rule 'more than 70% of your dots within 3 px of one registry raster's dots' returns DUPLICATE/STOP for any non-empty emission, because the 526-blob census contains universal-coverage lattice probes whose 3 px halo covers the whole eligible footprint. entries.status: resolved - writer changed, audit loop added, fit reads verified in-RAM copies
entries.title: Channel .npy files lost their first 4 KiB page AFTER a verified write, under the channel stage's load
entries.what_it_is: In the first H84 channel build, 16/81 files (all det_elev band) later had bytes 128-4095 zeroed (the rest of the header's first 4 KiB page = first 992 float32 values); the fit stage's digest guard refused them ('channel byte-integrity failure: COH_det_elev'). A second build, with save_verified hardened (fsync + POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED + re-read compare), passed every per-file verification yet an end-of-stage audit found 65/81 files changed. H82 saw the same signature (8/79). A quiet reproduction (4x np.save + 4x structural.save_array, 4.59M float32, 100 s) left 8/8 files intact. The shared feature store work/r2/features was audited: 78/78 feature_sha256 match, no zero-first-page column.
entries.how_we_know: byte comparison of the torn files against their in-memory arrays; manifest SHA-256 vs disk digest after cache drop; logs /tmp/h84_channels.log and /tmp/h84_fit.log of the failed runs.
entries.handling: scripts/run_h84.py stage_channels now writes through gems52.structural.save_array (atomic .partial + fsync + re-read + rename), then sleeps, drops the page cache per file, re-digests all 81 files against both the file digest and an array digest, and recomputes only bands with moved files (max 4 passes, else SystemExit). The fit stage loads every channel it needs fully into RAM (RamBank) after checking its array digest, so later on-disk changes cannot reach a model. run_h82.save_verified keeps the fsync + fadvise hardening.
entries.disposition: third build: audit pass 1 found 0/81 moved; fit read verified copies. Root cause (filesystem/VM page handling under memory pressure) not identified - recorded, not claimed.

entries.disposition: disclosed
entries.title: Band 10 (dist_to_eq) carries distances larger than the grid can physically contain
entries.what_it_is: Inside the footprint, band 10 of data/training_features.tif has median 622.8 m and p99 50.2 km, which are plausible, but a maximum of 4,962,515 m. The grid is 3730 x 3292 px at 100 m, so its diagonal is about 492 km; 0.41% of footprint pixels (21,326 of 5,165,840) exceed 329 km and are therefore impossible as a distance-to-nearest-earthquake measured on this grid.
entries.how_we_know: Read band 10 directly with rasterio, applied the official nodata sentinel filter, and took percentiles over the 5,165,840-px footprint: min 0.0, p1 118.3, p50 622.8, p99 50,237.2, max 4,962,515.0, with mean(v > 329000) = 0.0041287.
entries.handling: Layers derived from band 10 are rank-encoded before any learner sees them, so the tail is compressed to a single extreme rank rather than dominating a linear model; the layer A_eq_dist_negrank is kept but must not be read as a physical distance. Flagged because any future use of band 10 as a metres-valued quantity (a buffer, a threshold, a decay length) would silently mis-handle those pixels.

entries.disposition: fixed; rule recorded
entries.title: Indexing a 2-D fold grid with one 1-D coordinate array allocated ~4 GB and was killed by the OOM killer with no traceback
entries.what_it_is: cotrain_r5.fit_oof did fold[rows] and fold[cols] on a (3730, 3292) int16 grid. With one index array numpy selects whole ROWS, so each expression built a (300k, 3292) view and the fold test broadcast over the wrong axis. On a 3.9 GB box the process was SIGKILLed (exit 137) during stage 2 with no Python traceback, which reads exactly like a memory-hungry model rather than like a two-character indexing bug.
entries.how_we_know: dmesg is the only place this sandbox records an OOM kill (/sys/fs/cgroup/memory.* is not exposed and free/ps mislead), plus an RSS watchdog that put the last allocation at cotrain_r5.py:194. Re-validated after the fix: view A out-of-fold in 41 s at 1,113 MB peak.
entries.handling: Paired indexing fold[rows, cols] everywhere, with the reason in a comment at the call site. Regression test in tests/test_r5.py. Standing rule: never index a 2-D grid with a single 1-D coordinate array.
entries.evidence: src/gems52_r5/cotrain_r5.py::fit_oof, logs/r5_main.log (local artifact; logs/ is gitignored)
entries.provenance_warning: Cost two full pipeline runs to find; the failure mode is silence, not an exception.

entries.disposition: disclosed; published numbers are the reproducible ones
entries.title: Two runs of the same stage-3 code on the same on-disk fields logged different independence and A-only numbers, and both saved OOF fields carry 620 impossible zeros
entries.what_it_is: Run 1 logged spearman 0.15012 and A-only 43,604 px; run 2, loading the very files run 1 had just written, logged spearman 0.22757 and A-only 43,672 px. Separately, work/r5/oof_A.npy and oof_B.npy each hold 620 pixels with value 0.0 where they must be NaN: exactly row 0, columns 0-619, which is exactly the out-of-footprint prefix of the first row (valid turns True at column 620). Both files, same 620 pixels.
entries.how_we_know: Four checks, all in this checkout. (1) git diff 9bbcbf5..HEAD shows the only stage-3 code change between the two runs is inside pseudo_labels; independence, disagreement_strata and rank_within are untouched and RNG-free, and every input (cat 60,988 px, valid 5,165,840 px, legal 4,861,502 px, bid, pos, neg, seeded sample) is identical. (2) A fresh in-process recomputation from the saved arrays reproduces run 2 exactly (0.227574 spearman / 0.106752 pearson / A-only 43,672 / B-only 43,799). (3) The write path cannot touch those pixels: te_block = (fold == k) & valid, fold is -1 outside the footprint, and a fold-0 reproduction leaves the prefix fully NaN with no zero in its prediction vector. (4) np.save/np.load round-trips are exact here: a deterministic pattern, a NaN-heavy field, a re-save of oof_A.npy and two loads of it all agree bit for bit, so this is not file I/O. The mechanism is therefore unidentified.
entries.handling: Run 1's stage-3 log line is marked superseded and is not quoted anywhere in evidence/, docs/ or the site; every published stage-3 number comes from the arrays on disk and reproduces. The 620 pixels are outside the footprint, so no consumer can see them: rank_within masks to pos|neg, legal is a subset of valid, and the emission is a subset of legal. Bounded, not explained, and not papered over.
entries.provenance_warning: Any future stage-3 number must be recomputed from the saved fields and compared with the log before it is quoted.

entries.disposition: rule corrected against an official answer
entries.title: The organiser states the known-fault mask is pixel-exact and that new-fault truth may lie within 300 m of a known trace, which contradicts this repo's blanket 'emit nothing within 200 m of a mapped trace' rule
entries.what_it_is: DrivenData staff (chrisk-dd, topic 11516, 2026-09-16 and 2026-09-21): known USGS/INGENIOUS fault pixels are masked out of evaluation in both rounds; 'the mask is indeed pixel-exact - it is identical to the provided set of training fault labels'; a predicted pixel near a known trace but far from new-fault truth 'will be fully penalized, i.e., the buffer does not apply to known faults'; and 'a new-fault ground truth pixel can indeed lie within 300m of a known fault trace. Such pixels would constitute corrections or modifications to existing fault traces. Identifying these corrections is one outcome we are aiming for.' knowledge/10 §2 turned a local measurement into the blanket rule 'emit nothing inside 200 m of a mapped trace' and called it the largest measured effect in the repo's history.
entries.how_we_know: Official forum answers at https://community.drivendata.org/t/11516 plus the problem description's own sentence that 'portions of the existing fault data may be misaligned from the true location of the surface fault, which is the prediction target'. Against the bytes: the 6,436 px that separate gems24-d2-8 (0.2600) from the champion (0.2778) are all 100-200 m from the catalogue, i.e. NOT masked, so they paid full false-positive tax; solving T_B - T_A = 200.62 - 0.01424|G| with |G| in the independent bracket [8,128, 15,179] bounds the credit those ring pixels earned at 0-85 over 6,436 px, a density of 0.0132 against 0.0279 for uniform random.
entries.handling: The rule is restated where it is used: the 100-200 m corridor is dead mass FOR THIS FAMILY'S HABITAT FIELD, which hugs mapped traces, and that measurement does not generalise to a detector aimed at trace corrections. knowledge/32 R5-H1 proposes exactly that detector and states the risk that the corridor is genuinely empty. The emitted R5 file still excludes the 200 m ring, so this correction costs nothing in the shipped artifact and is recorded as the top-ranked next experiment rather than as a silent re-tune.
entries.provenance_warning: Forum answers are staff statements, not a scoring receipt; the mask geometry was never observed directly.

The gain came from the other 6,436 deleted pixels, which are 100-200 m off the catalogue, are not masked, and are pure false-positive mass.

The two accounts are reconcilable: A emits 40,199 px of which 2,545 are masked, B emits 46,635 of which the same 2,545 are masked, and the evaluated difference is 6,436.

entries.disposition: disclosed; do not build on the missing layer
entries.title: The organiser's feature list promises a top-of-crustal magnetic source depth estimate that no band in training_features.tif corresponds to
entries.what_it_is: Page 967 lists the magnetics as 'reduced-to-pole magnetic anomaly, total magnetic intensity, the vertical and horizontal slope of total magnetic intensity, and the top-of-crustal magnetic source depth estimate'. The five magnetic bands in the file are mag_anom (1), rtp (2), tmi_hg (3), tmi_vg (9) and tmi (14) -- anomaly, RTP, TMI and its two gradients. None is a source-depth estimate, and no band of any category is described as one. The two remaining unaccounted bands, deq_n100a15 (10) and ieq_n100a15 (16), are the INGENIOUS earthquake-rate-density layers per staff (forum topic 11557).
entries.how_we_know: All 19 band descriptions and their data_category tags were read out of the delivered file with rasterio this session and are quoted verbatim in knowledge/25 §6; the organiser's list is quoted from page 967 fetched 2026-10-08. Band 6 is the mirror-image defect and is already recorded: its tag says tilt angle, its bytes are radiometric total count (Spearman +1.0000 with the GeoDAWN total-count grid, IR-52-034).
entries.handling: No R5 hypothesis or layer uses a magnetic source-depth product, because it does not exist in the delivered data. knowledge/32 records this explicitly so a future round does not invent one from band 10, whose values run to ~4.96e6 and which is a distance to earthquake, not a depth. If the layer matters, the route is a question on the forum, not a guess.
entries.provenance_warning: The organiser's own prose and the organiser's own file disagree; neither is a scoring receipt.

entries.what_it_is: 30 of 102 H91 channel files failed run_h82.Bank's byte-integrity guard (ValueError: channel byte-integrity failure) after run_h82.save_verified had already written them, read them back and recorded a matching digest. The files that failed were not the same set on each attempt: the first pass named CSA_det_elev_dirR_l2, the second CSA_iso_grav_anom_hg_dirR_l2, so the whole original channels pass is suspect, not three files.
entries.how_we_know: the manifest digests recorded at write time were re-hashed against the bytes on disk; 30 of 102 disagreed on the first three bands processed. run_h82.Bank re-hashes every column it is asked to gather and refuses to train on a mismatch, which is the guard working as designed. evidence/h91_preflight_integrity.json records the original mismatch set.
entries.title: 30 of 102 H91 channel files failed the byte-integrity guard after passing it
entries.detail: run_h82.save_verified wrote each channel, read it back, required a bit-exact match and recorded the digest; a later re-hash found 30 files (the first three bands processed) whose bytes no longer matched. run_h82.Bank refused to train on them (ValueError: channel byte-integrity failure), which is the guard working. The mechanism is IR-H82-002: a torn write against a filesystem that snapshots concurrently, landing after the verification pass rather than during it.
entries.resolution: scripts/repair_h91_channels.py recomputed the affected (band, lag) channels from the pinned rasters with the same arithmetic, wrote them with an added digest-stability check (two digests separated by a pause), re-hashed every file on disk into the manifest, and re-verified the whole bank. No value was patched by hand and no channel was dropped.
entries.disposition: bank recomputed in full by scripts/repair_h91_channels.py --all and re-verified; the corruption mechanism itself is environment-level (IR-H82-002) and is NOT fixed at the repository level, so every future channel build must run the repair before fitting. No value was patched by hand and no channel was dropped.
entries.status: resolved; mechanism still open (environment-level, not repository-level)

entries.title: View B omits band 6, which is radiometric by content despite its magnetic tag
entries.what_it_is: training_features.tif band 6 is tagged 'tc' (tilt angle / total curvature, magnetic). Its content is total-count radiometric. The lane brief asks View B to include the radiometric bands of training_features.tif. H94 used the external GeoDAWN layers instead and left band 6 out, a declared deviation in knowledge/80 §1. The sentinel is a second data-hygiene fact: any code that reads band 6 without masking −3.4028e38 gets wrong statistics.
entries.how_we_know: Re-read from disk this session. Band 6 (training_features.tif) carries a declared nodata value of −3.4028e38 on 7,113,320 cells. On the 5,165,840 non-sentinel cells, Pearson with GeoDAWN TC (geodawn_rad_u8 band 4) is 0.99569 and Spearman is 0.99912. On the 5,164,300 GeoDAWN-footprint cells, Pearson is 0.99714 and Spearman 0.99995. Without the sentinel mask the Pearson value is meaningless (about 0.886 on the full grid). H61 already isolates band 6 in View B (scripts/run_h61.py setup).

entries.title: H93 dots lane: near-3px 0.7275 vs own H83-E3 prior; random control 0.20 confirms real overlap
entries.what_it_is: The H93 emission's dots-phase lane gate measured 72.75% of dots within 3 px of gems52-h83-offcatalogue-cotrain-37654px-e3 (policy verdict DUPLICATE/STOP). entries.title: Lane dots literal DUPLICATE/STOP fires only against the universal-coverage probe r13-lattice
entries.status: reported, not waived (same class as IR-H85-009)
entries.what_it_is: The H95 final dots trigger the brief's literal lane rule (near-3px fraction 0.9993 vs data/scored/13gems_20261001_r13-lattice-s5_v2_nan-outside.tif). That raster is a 206,895-positive universal-coverage probe: uniformly random dots of the same budget score 0.9991 against it (H85 measured), so the literal rule cannot distinguish any localised raster from drift. Excluding probes (the shared gates lane_report 'policy' verdict), H95's maximum near-3px fraction is 0.5233 (vs the H87 sibling raster) and maximum Spearman is 0.0356, both inside the 0.70 / 0.90 bars. Surface-phase lane: PASS both verdicts (max Spearman 0.0914).
entries.how_we_know: evidence/h95_lane_dots.json and evidence/h95_lane_surface.json (gems52.gates.lane_report, exact lattice <=3 px proximity, analytic phi for binary priors); probe classification by measured 3px coverage in the same receipts.
entries.disposition: Both verdicts published side by side; policy verdict is used for the drift judgement and the literal verdict is disclosed in the run card.

entries.title: Frozen H95 field formula had a veto-rank flaw; amended pre-fit
entries.status: closed - amendment written before any fit (registry/h95_amendment_veto.json)
entries.what_it_is: The frozen veto term veto=rank01(clip(b-a,0,1)) assigns mid-ranks to the ~50% zero support, so A-dominant (buried-target) pixels would receive a spurious veto penalty meant for B-only cells. Found by reading the formula against the shared rank01 implementation before any view was computed.
entries.how_we_know: registry/h95_preregistration.json hash 0f664c43... is unchanged; the amendment (hash 91f74c5a...) freezes veto=rank01 on the positive support only, 0 elsewhere. knowledge/80a_amendment_H95_veto_positive_support.md records the reasoning and voids itself if any fit predates 2026-10-10T22:12:00Z.
entries.disposition: Original registration preserved; both hashes pinned in scripts/run_h95_cotrain_bidir.py which refuses to run if either moves.

entries.title: Same evaluator version, two withheld-positive tallies across rounds (53,186 vs 60,894)
entries.what_it_is: Receipts under gems52-pooled-hide-v1 report withheld_positive_px = 53,186 (H82, H84, H85) and 60,894 (H86, H86-E, H95). In gems52.spatial.folds, truth = held_all & region, so the summed tally equals the catalogue pixels inside each round's eligible footprint. 60,894 is the all-19-bands-finite catalogue count (IR-45-001); 53,186 implies an eligible mask that excluded ~7,708 further catalogue pixels (most plausibly external-layer nodata holes in the H82 FeatureStore build). The metric is identical; the fold tally is not.
entries.how_we_know: src/gems52/spatial.py folds() (truth = held_all & region) read this session; evidence/h82_holdout.json, h84_run_card.json, h85_holdout.json, h86_holdout.json, h86_euler_holdout.json, h95_holdout.json read this session.
entries.disposition: Within-round arm comparisons are valid. entries.title: Emission rank domain was not fixed in the H97 preregistration
entries.what_it_is: The preregistered formula is fixed; the rank domain is not. The holdout ranks a and b inside each fold's allowed cells (as H84 does). The emission field ranks them over the stitched per-fold ranks on the emission pool (h82.stitch convention, scripts/run_h97.py stage_build). Both use the same formula and weights.
entries.how_we_know: evidence/h97_build.json rank_domain field; scripts/run_h97.py stage_build comment.
entries.disposition: Disclosed. Future rounds must put the rank domain in the preregistration before the fit.

entries.title: Git Data API secondary rate limit blocked the prior census; codeload fallback added to the shared tool
entries.status: closed - fallback added and verified; census complete
entries.what_it_is: During the H97 session, api.github.com returned HTTP 403 ('API rate limit exceeded ... scraping') for blob reads from 418 of 526 census blobs, after 108 succeeded. The core REST quota was not exhausted (remaining 5000), so this is the secondary limit. scripts/fetch_prior_inventory.py now reads each blob from the codeload.github.com archive at the census's pinned commit and accepts it only if the git blob SHA-1 equals the census blob id and the byte count matches. The Git Data API is the fallback.

entries.title: Dot-lane literal DUPLICATE is driven by high-coverage non-probe rasters; random dots fail the same way
entries.status: open - flagged for owner review; verdict kept as recorded
entries.what_it_is: Full-census dots lane: literal DUPLICATE/STOP, max 3 px share 1.0 (universal-coverage probes, which the policy excludes by design). Policy DUPLICATE/STOP, max 3 px share 0.8773 against gems-cleanup-a-20260928T195952Z-curv_scarp.tif (coverage of the eligible footprint 0.8976). Other informative offenders: 0.8493, 0.8236, 0.7600 (coverage 0.835-0.862). The probe threshold PROBE_COVERAGE = 0.95 is preregistered and does not exclude these rasters. Chance control (same count, uniform over the emission pool, seed 97, same 3 px disk): random dots score 0.8959 on the 0.8976-coverage raster, above H97's 0.8773.
